1.1: Behold my son, I have caused to come into your hands a fragment of the writings of Aḇraham in which he has left a record of his sojourn among men and of the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 unto him. This I have brought to you that you might restore that which is lost that the fullness of the record in its original purity might be found again among the sons of Elohim.
1.2: Behold, these things are qodesh, wherefore, send them not forth unto the children of men but let them be for the edification of the elect that your hearts may be turned unto the Fathers and you may draw close to them and they to you.
1.3: Thus will the veil be withdrawn and you will commune with the General Assembly of the First-born and shall even be ushered back unto my presence.
1.4: Go now and do this work which I have placed in thine hands. Amĕn.

10.1: And the child grew and waxed strong in wisdom and mighty in the power of the kehunnah for he was initiated into the Order of the Ancients in his childhood and learned the rites and ordinances and the powers of the kehunnah with the signs and tokens and key words wherewith he could call upon the powers of the shamayim to combat the forces of the adversary.
10.2: And when he was come of age, he took twelve wives and begat many sons and daughters who grew up in righteousness and served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all their days and some died and others were caught up unto the city of Ḥanoḵ.
10.3: But in the next generation they corrupted themselves, for the daughters of Noaḥ’s sons did go forth and lay with the sons of men, which thing was an abomination in the eyes of Elohim.
10.4: Wherefore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said unto Noaḥ, Behold, the daughters of your sons have sold themselves, for behold, My anger is kindled against the sons of men, for they will not hearken to My voice; wherefore, all those who go in unto them will be destroyed with them.

100.1: After these things Elohim appeared to me in a vision and He said to me, Behold Aḇraham, it is ten full years since you came into this land from Ḥaran.
100.2: Two years did you remain then in the land, seven years you were in Mitsrayim and one year has passed since your return from Mitsrayim.
100.3: Now, number all that you have and see how it has increased to double that which went out with you in the day you came forth from Ḥaran.
100.4: Therefore, fear not, for I am with you and will be your help and the source of your strength.
100.5: I will be your shield and your exceeding great reward and your wealth and your possessions shall I increase exceedingly.

101.1: And I said to Him, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 My Elohim, truly my wealth and my possessions have increased, but behold, Eli’ezer of Dammeseq stand as my heir, whereas, prior to my departure from the city of Shalom, father Shĕm said unto me, Eli’ezer is a good and righteous man and he shall be greatly baruḵ in time and in eternity, but he shall not be your heir, for another shall be your heir who shall come forth from the womb of your wife whom you shall take in the house of your father for she is ordained to be your queen of queens and the mother of your heir.
101.2: Wherefore then does Sarah remain barren, having neither son nor daughter?
101.3: No, replied Elohim, fear not, for none shall be your heir except he that shall come forth from the womb of your wife Sarah for she is ordained to be your queen of queens and the mother of your heir.
101.4: Therefore is her name called Sarah.

102.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 took me out of the camp and He said, Look now toward the shamayim and tell the stars, if you be able to number them.
102.2: And He said to me, So shall your seed be.
102.3: And I said to him, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, how will You give me this land for an everlasting inheritance?
102.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 replied, Though you were dead, am I not able to give it to you?
102.5: And if you shall die, yet you shall possess it, for the day comes that the Bĕn of Aḏam shall live but how can He live if He be not dead?
102.7: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 touched the eyes of my understanding that they were opened and I beheld the days of the Bĕn of Aḏam, for I beheld Him ministering to my seed, teaching them the Torah of Elohim, healing the sick, casting out devils and doing many wonderful works.
102.8: I saw also the Bĕn of Aḏam lifted up upon the stake for the sins of men; wherefore I wept for the wickedness of man which could impale the Bĕn of Elohim.
102.9: Nevertheless, I saw also that He should rise again from the dead, wherein my heart did rejoice and my being found rest in the knowledge that though I should die, yet again in the flesh should I see Elohim and dwell in the land of my inheritance.
102.10: For I saw also the days of the coming of the Bĕn of Aḏam upon the earth in the last days when He shall descend with ten thousands of His qodeshim according to the neḇuah of father Ḥanoḵ and the earth shall be cleansed by fire.
102.11: Then all shall rise to stand before Elohim, both the just and the unjust, to be judged according to their works.

103.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, saved you from the fire in the land of Shin’ar and from the hand of the wicked priest and from all the evil intentions of Meleḵ Nimroḏ and I brought you into this land that I might give it to you as an everlasting inheritance.
103.2: Now, I knew that the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was true. Nevertheless, I desired to know more of this inheritance which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had provided me.
103.3: Wherefore, I said, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, how shall it be that I shall inherit this land wherein I am a stranger?
103.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, Take Me a heifer of three years old and a she goat of three years old and a ram of three years old and a turtle dove and a young pigeon.
103.5: Divide each of these in the midst and lay one half on each side of an open place, except the birds you shall not divide but lay one on each side.
103.6: Wherefore, I went and did according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded me and when the fowls came down upon the carcasses, I drove them away.
103.7: And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon me and lo, in the sleep was a great horror of darkness.
103.8: And I cried unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, what means this great horror of darkness?
103.9: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land which shall not be theirs and shall be in bondage to strangers, even to the seed of Ḥam who shall again overrun the land of Mitsrayim.
103.10: And your seed shall be afflicted and serve them four hundred years.
103.11: But at that time, I shall judge the seed of Ḥam and your seed shall come up out of the land of Mitsrayim with great substance.
103.12: And as for you, you shall die and go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried in a good old age.
103.13: But in the fourth generation your seed shall come higher again for the iniquity of the Kena’anites is not yet full.

104.1: And it came to pass that when the sun was down and it was dark, behold, two personages passed between those pieces which I had divided.
104.2: And their countenance was as fire such that I could hardly look upon them and the one said to me, Behold, of your seed shall ha’Mashiaḥ come who shall redeem all those who believe on His Name and walk in His footsteps.
104.3: Wherefore, repent and call upon the Name of the Bĕn all your days that in the end you may dwell with Me in My mansion.

105.1: Now when Sarah saw that she bare neither son nor daughter, it grieved her heart.
105.2: And she said to me, Take therefore Haḡar, daughter of Pharaoh, to be your wife, for she is a woman now.
105.3: And let her come into my bed and let her womb be to you in the place of mine to raise up seed to you.
105.4: Haḡar also was willing to enter this covenant and it was according to the voice of the Ruaḥ of Elohim; wherefore, Sarah gave Haḡar to be my wife and Sarah and Haḡar were as one wife to that the seed of Haḡar might be also the seed of Sarah.
105.5: For Haḡar had been raised by Sarah and been taught by her and had followed Sarah in ways of righteousness.

106.1: And when I came into Haḡar in Sarah’s bed, she conceived.
106.2: And when Haḡar saw that she had conceived, she rejoiced greatly and began to be lifted up in pride and to despise Sarah and she taunted Sarah, saying, Surely I am better than you for in all the years your master has lain with you, you have not conceived, but lo, in this short time, I have conceived from the seed of my master.
106.3: And Sarah was grieved in her heart and she said to me, Surely Haḡar has wronged me and you also have contributed to her wrong, for she has spoken despitefully to me in your presence, yet you have done nothing to correct her.
106.4: But I replied to Sarah, Surely Haḡar is your child for you have instructed her from her youth.
106.5: Correct her, therefore, as seems good to you.

107.1: However, when Sarah attempted to correct Haḡar, Haḡar grew angry and determined to return to her father’s people; wherefore, she departed into the wilderness.
107.2: But a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 met her by a well where she stopped to rest and he said to her, Haḡar, daughter of Sarah, who gave you to her husband Aḇraham and took you into her own bed that you might raise up seed to her, why are you fleeing into the wilderness from the camp of Aḇraham?
107.3: And Haḡar replied, I am returning to the land of my father for it grieved me to be bound to Sarah.
107.4: And the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to her, Return to Sarah and be subject to her for she is given to you to be a mother to you and this seed is hers as well as yours.
107.5: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will multiply your seed exceedingly so that it shall not be numbered for multitude and you shall bear a son and shall call his name Yishma’ĕl, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has heard your prayers and answered them.
107.6: He will be a man of the desert and a man of war; nevertheless, many shall join themselves to him and his people shall be great.

108.1: Haḡar replied, What shall I say is the name of him who bears these glad tidings.
108.2: And the messenger replied, Be’ĕr Laḥai Ro’i, for know that Elohim sees you in all places whithersoever you shall be.
108.3: And Haḡar said, I know that Elohim sees me, for He has this day sent His messenger to minister to me.
108.4: Wherefore, Haḡar returned to the tent of Sarah and at the appointed time she bare to me a son and I called his name Yishma’ĕl, according to the word of the messenger.
108.5: And I was four score and six years old when Haḡar bare Yishma’ĕl to me.

109.1: At the end of thirteen years, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to me and He said to me, Aḇraham, because you have been faithful in all things to me from the time you were three years old, and behold, now you are ninety and nine, therefore, I will establish My Covenant with you for with you I shall commence a new dispensation of the Besorah that from this time forth all those who would be sealed into Me must be sealed into you.
109.2: Wherefore, I will send Noaḥ to you in the Mishkan, and he will bestow upon you the keys of this kehunnah, for the city of Malkitseḏeq will I take up from off the earth and there will be a new beginning in you.
109.3: For I will greatly multiply your seed and I will make them My ministers that through your kehunnah all the peoples of the earth shall be baruḵ.
109.4: Therefore, from this time forth shall every male child among you be circumcised in that his foreskin shall be opened in token of the opening of his heart to the light of the Besorah.
109.5: And on the eighth day shall you do it that you may remember that on the eighth day they shall be immersed that the beraḵah of the Besorah may come upon them.
109.6: This is according to the Covenant I made with Aḏam in the garden Ĕḏen, but I instructed Noaḥ and Shĕm not to administer this Covenant to you that you might receive it in token of this new Covenant which I make with you.
109.7: Although I gave these ordinances in the beginning to Aḏam, yet the sons of men have continually gone astray from my precepts and have not kept My ordinances which I gave to their fathers.
109.8: They have neglected the ordinance of immersion which I commanded unto them in token of the burial of the natural man and have ceased to receive the anointing whereby they become melaḵim and kohĕn unto me.
109.9: Yea, they have turned from My Commandments and changed My ordinances and have replaced immersion with the washing of children which they call immersion.
109.10: But, behold, this is no immersion, for I will atone for the fall of Aḏam; wherefore, little children are innocent until they reach the age of accountability.
109.11: But the sons of men have rejected My atonement wherein I will offer My Only Begotten Bĕn for the sins of the world, for they say that the blood of righteous Heḇel as shed for sins, thereby rejecting Me as their Savior.
109.12: But you have upheld My ordinances. Therefore, you seed shall sprinkle all nations, for you shall be a father of many nations.
109.13: And you shall be fruitful and many nations shall come of you and melaḵim of nations shall be of your seed.
109.14: Moreover, you shall not cut yourselves in your foreskins after the manner of the heathen, for this is the lesser law and applied only to those who have had part of the Besorah cut off from that which they have received.
109.15: But your hearts are opened to the fullness of My Besorah wherefore your foreskins shall be opened.
109.16: For if it were profitable for you to be without a foreskin, then would your father beget you in your mother without a foreskin.
109.17: Take not away what Elohim has given.
109.18: But let your foreskins be opened, for this is the true circumcision and it will be profitable to you as a covenant written in your flesh, which shall be an everlasting Covenant.
109.19: Your daughters also shall be circumcised upon the marriage bed when the matrix is opened by the entrance of her husband, for this is a qodesh ordinance, and it is completed at the birth of her first-born; wherefore it is written that the first-born which opened the matrix is qodesh because it is an instrument in the performance of a qodesh ordinance.
109.20: Now, go into the Mishkan and fast and pray until Noaḥ comes to bestow upon you the keys of which I have spoken.

11.1: And when Noaḥ was four hundred and fifty years old, he begat a son and he called his name Yepheth.
11.2: Forty-two years later he begat another son of her who was the mother of Yepheth, and he called his name Shĕm.
11.3: Eight years later Noaḥ begat a son of his wife Na’amah, who was of the seed of Qayin, and he called his name Ḥam, for he said, Through him will the curse be preserved in the land.

110.1: When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had departed from me, I went into the Mishkan and I remained there fasting and praying for three days.
110.2: And at the end of that time Noaḥ came to me and he said, Hail, Aḇraham, for you are highly favored of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
110.3: Behold, I come to you from the city of Ḥanoḵ my father to bestow upon you the keys which I received from Ḥanoḵ many years ago, for you shall stand at the head and your posterity shall be without number and in you and in your seed after you shall all the nations of the earth be baruḵ.
110.4: When Noaḥ had departed from me, I rose up and was circumcised by Eli’ezer and all the males of my house were circumcised with me, including my son Yishma’ĕl who was thirteen years old at this time.
110.5: And I conferred upon my son Yishma’ĕl the Kehunnah of Elias and ordained him to be a kohĕn that he might minister before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
110.6: But Yishma’ĕl did not honor his kehunnah, taking it to be a light thing, which thing was a grief of heart to me for I knew that in the shamayim he was counted as having no kehunnah because he honored it not; wherefore, I did not call upon him to act in the kohenim office.

111.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to me in the plains of Mamrĕ and he said to me, Behold, Yishma’ĕl shall not be your heir, neither Eli’ezer, for Sarah will I baraḵ and I will give you a son of her.
111.2: She shall be the mother of nations and melaḵim and people shall be of her.
111.3: Then I fell upon my face before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and I rejoiced and I said to Him, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, it is a wondrous thing that this promise should be fulfilled when I am a hundred years old and Sarah is ninety.
111.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, Prepare your heart to receive it, and He told me many secret things concerning the conception of the child which are great mysteries to the unenlightened, but the elect shall know them, and I rejoiced therein.

112.1: When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had told me these things, I thought of my son Yishma’ĕl and I prayed, O Elohim, grant that Yishma’ĕl might live uprightly before You.
112.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim replied, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son and you shall call his name Yitsḥaq and I will continue in him the Covenant which I have established with you to be an everlasting Covenant with his seed after him.
112.3: And as for Yishma’ĕl, I have heard you.
112.4: Behold, I have baraḵ him and will make him a great nation.
112.5: But My Covenant will I establish with Yitsḥaq whom Sarah shall bear to you at this same time in the next year.
112.6: Then Elohim left me and I saw Him ascend up into the shamayim and my heart rejoiced in the promises of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to me.

113.1: Three months later 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent to me three of His ministering messengers who were qodesh men of Elohim from the city of Ḥanoḵ.
113.2: For I was sitting at the door of my tent and I lifted up my eyes from my meditations, and behold, three men in the distance were walking toward our camp.
113.3: And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 whispered to me that they were qodesh men of Elohim who had a beraḵah for me; wherefore, I rose up and ran to meet them; and bowing down before them, I led them to Sarah’s tent.
113.4: Taking water from Sarah, I washed their feet and spreading a carpet under the tree which was at the door of Sarah’s tent, I spread cushions upon it and caused them to sit down there.
113.5: And I called Eli’ezer and instructed him to send one of the young men to fetch a young and tender calf and supervise the preparation of it.
113.6: Sarah also supervised the young women in preparing cakes and milk and cheese, mutton and beef to eat until the calf was prepared.

114.1: When they had eaten, one of the qodesh men said to me, We shall return to you nine months, and behold, at that time Sarah shall bear a son.
114.2: Now, Sarah was listening at the door of the tent, and when she heard these words, she laughed within herself, knowing that she was past the age of bearing and I also was very old.
114.3: But the qodesh man of Elohim rebuked her, saying, Is anything too hard for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
114.4: Surely when we return here in nine months, you shall bear a son.
114.5: Whereupon the three qodesh men of Elohim entered with me into Sarah’s tent and baraḵ her.
114.6: And the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh fell upon Sarah in mighty power in the beraḵah and she conceived according to the word of the man of Elohim.

115.1: Then the three qodesh men of Elohim departed from our camp, and I walked with them to bring them on their way toward Seḏom.
115.2: And the one who had before spoken, said to me, Aḇraham, we are from the city of Ḥanoḵ and are ordained after the qodesh order of Elohim.
115.3: We have come not only to baraḵ Sarah that you might have seed raised up to you out of her, but also on a mission which brings us sorrow.
115.4: Nevertheless, the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me saying, Shall I hide from Aḇraham that thing which I will do?
115.5: No, surely for his integrity he shall know what I am about to do.
115.6: Wherefore, Aḇraham, have you looked upon the iniquities of Seḏom and her sister cities?
115.7: For they have provoked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with their abominations.
115.8: For four times in each year they gather together to sing and dance before their mighty ones and when they are dancing every man lays hold upon the wives and daughters of his neighbors and lies with them and this they do without authority from Elohim, which thing is an abomination in His sight.
115.9: But, behold, this is the least of their sins.
115.10: For no man is safe who enters their city, for when a stranger enters there, they will take from him his goods by force and they will abuse his body, for both men and women will they bind and crowds of the Seḏomites will gather about them and lie with them by force until everyone who desire to lie with them has done so.
115.11: Now it is a wicked thing that men or women should be forced to lie with another against their will, but here the whole city united to force this wicked thing.
115.12: Moreover, when they have stolen a man’s goods and abused his flesh, they will torture him and when they tire of torturing him, they will leave him naked and without food or water to die in the streets of their city and it is forbidden by the law for anyone to help such a one by giving him food or drink.
115.13: Moreover, the people of these cities have numerous mighty ones before which they practice every kind of abomination without authority.
115.14: Wherefore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent us to gather the righteous out of the cities before they are destroyed.
115.15: So saying, the three embraced me and kissed me and went on their way toward Seḏom.

116.1: But I remained a long time where they had departed from me thinking on the things they had said, for it grieved my heart that these great cities with all their inhabitants should be destroyed.
116.2: Wherefore, I, too, went down to the vicinity of Seḏom and I called upon the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 there.
116.3: And when He answered me out of the shamayim, I said to Him, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, merciful and kind, will You destroy the inheritances of the righteous because of the wicked?
116.4: No, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, far be it from You to do this thing. Will You not spare the inheritances of the righteous?
116.5: Peradventure there may be fifty righteous in the city, will You in Your anger destroy the city and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous that are in it?
116.6: Surely You will not destroy the inheritances of the righteous because of the wicked.
116.7: Such a judgment should never be passed according to the justice of Your Qodesh Torah which is in Your bosom.
116.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, If I find in these cities fifty righteous who keep the Torah and precepts of Elohim and have not partaken of the abominations of the Seḏomites, then surely I will spare the whole country for their sake.

117.1: Nevertheless, I ventured to speak before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 again, for I know that all His Ways are just.
117.2: And I said unto Him, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, suppose there shall lack but five of the fifty righteous. Will You destroy the whole land for the lack of five men?
117.3: And He said, If there be forty-five righteous in the land, I will not destroy it.
117.4: And I spake to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 again, saying, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I know that I am yet but dust and ashes, for although I am, by the testimony of Your own mouth, declared to be a son of Elohim, yet I am not yet esteemed to be like You.
117.5: Nevertheless, be not displeased with me when I plead on behalf of the righteous; for suppose there shall be forty righteous in the land?
117.6: And He said, I will not destroy it if I find there forty.
117.7: Then I said, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You have been patient indeed with Your servant; wherefore, I shall speak yet again before You, Suppose there shall thirty righteous be found there?
117.8: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 replied, I will not destroy it if I find thirty there.
117.9: Then I spake again saying, I have ventured to speak before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; shall I now cease lest the righteous be destroyed with the wicked?
117.10: Suppose there shall be twenty righteous found in the land?
117.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.
117.12: Finally I said, O, let not 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be displeased and I will speak only once more.
117.13: Suppose ten righteous shall be found there?
117.14: And He said, I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.
117.15: But you, Aḇraham, remain here in prayer and fasting until My messengers return to you, for if ten righteous be not found in the land, I shall gather out those righteous who are found there and you shall be caught up of the earth to call down fire and brimstone upon the land by a qodesh ordinance inasmuch as you are a kohĕn and a meleḵ forever after the order of the Most High Elohim, having the right of the First-born which has come down from the fathers to exercise absolute authority over your posterity, even the right of life and death under the direction of the Qodesh One.
117.16: Nevertheless, remember that this authority can only be exercised under the direction of the shamayim, for when any man exercises his kehunnah contrary to the will of the shamayim, his kehunnah is forfeited, his authority passed away and he can call upon the powers of the shamayim to accomplish no work from that day forward.
117.17: Wherefore, let all men repent of the exercise of unrighteous dominion and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, that they be severed not from the rights of His House.
117.18: So saying, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 departed from me and I remained in that place in fasting and praying, awaiting the return of the three messengers.

118.1: This is the account which Lot told to me, Aḇraham, concerning the coming of the three messengers to him in Seḏom.
118.2: For Lot was sitting in the door of his house in the city of Seḏom conversing with two of his sons-in-law who were Seḏomites, when he saw three men approaching down the street of the city.
118.3: And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 whispered to Lot, Behold these are My messengers who bring tidings of deliverance.
118.4: Lot, therefore, rose up to meet them and bowing down before them, said, Behold now, my masters, turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house and tarry all night that I may wash your feet and anoint your heads and feed you, and in the morning you may go on leaving only a beraḵah upon the head of your servant.
118.5: And they said, No, but we will abide in the street tonight for we have heard that it is not safe to enter into the house of a Seḏomite lest we be abused and tortured and killed and our property stolen from us.
118.6: But Lot replied, Not so, my masters, for I am no Seḏomite, but a true worshiper of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and I know that you are His messengers for His Ruaḥ has shown me this thing.
118.7: Then, when Lot had confessed his faith in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the messengers entered with him into his house and he did set before them a feast with unleavened bread and wine and they baraḵ it and partook thereof and Lot’s family also partook and were filled.

119.1: When Lot’s two sons-in-law saw him take the strangers into his home, they went straightway to the magistrates of the city for it was unlawful in the city of Seḏom to entertain a stranger in your home.
119.2: Wherefore, the people of Seḏom surrounded Lot’s house, both young and old, all the people of the city.
119.3: And one of them called to Lot and said, Where are the men whom you took into your house tonight?
119.4: Behold, you know that it is contrary to our laws to entertain strangers.
119.5: Nevertheless, we will forgive you for you are a mighty prince among us; therefore, bring forth the men to us that we may lie with them and do to them according to all the desires of our hearts.
119.6: But Lot went out the door to the front of his house and securing the door behind him, he confronted the Seḏomites.
119.7: And Lot said to them, I pray you, my brethren, do not do these wicked things, for it is contrary to the Torah of the Most High Elohim who is Meleḵ over all, to force anyone to lie with another.
119.8: Repent now, therefore, that the wrath of the Most High Elohim fall not upon you and you with your city be destroyed.
119.9: But they were angry with Lot and they cried to him, Stand away from the door lest we take you also.
119.10: You have come in among us and partaken of the good of our land and we have treated you with honor although you were a stranger. Do you now make yourself a judge over us?
119.11: And their anger increased against Lot and they said to him, Behold, we will deal worse with you than with them.
119.12: Wherefore, we shall take you and your daughters and the men who have come in to you and any others in your household who shall please us and we will do with you according to all our desires.
119.13: But Lot replied, Behold now, I have two daughters who have not lain with man.
119.14: Let me, I pray you, plead with you that you take them not according to this wickedness and abuse them according to your abominations, for the Most High Elohim will surely destroy this city if ye repent not.
119.15: Wherefore, you shall do nothing to me nor my daughters nor the strangers that are within my gate nor any of my household, for Elohim will smite you in the attempt.
119.16: And their anger increased yet more against Lot and they came near to break down the door, but the messengers of Elohim who were qodesh men bearing the Power of the Kehunnah after Elohim’s qodesh order, put forth their hands, pulled Lot into the house and shut the door behind him.
119.17: Then they smote the people of Seḏom with blindness so that they could not find the door.

12.1: Now Noaḥ had taken a wife of the seed of Qayin, and she was a righteous woman; nevertheless, the curse remained with her seed according to the word of Elohim.
12.2: And Noaḥ took her on this wise: For the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came unto Noaḥ, saying, Take for yourself Na’amah, the daughter of Lemeḵ, who dwells here in the city of your fathers, for she has been faithful to My Besorah, wherefore I shall preserve through her the seed of Qayin through the flood.
12.3: This Lemeḵ who was the father of Na’amah was of the seed of Qayin being the son of Methusa’ĕl, the son of Meḥuya’ĕl, the son of Iraḏ, the son of Ḥanoḵ, the son of Qayin.
12.4: Lemeḵ had married Aḏah and Tsillah, the daughters of Kena’an, the son of Enosh, the son of Shĕth, the son of Aḏam. Aḏah bare children unto Lemeḵ, but Tsillah was barren until her old age when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opened her womb, and she conceived and bare a son and a daughter.
12.5: Her son she named Tuḇal-Qayin, saying, After I had withered away have I obtained him from the Almighty Elohim.
12.6: Her daughter she named Na’amah, saying, After I had withered away have I obtained pleasure and delight.

120.1: And one of these qodesh men said to Lot, Take now all that appertain to you, whether persons or goods, out of this city, for the wrath of Elohim is upon this place and tomorrow it shall be destroyed because the cries of those who have been abused here have risen to the ears of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Tsebaoth and the abominations of the Seḏomites have come up before His face.
120.2: Wherefore, surely upon the morrow the vengeance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fall upon Seḏom that neither root nor branch shall be left here for the fullness of their iniquity has come upon them and in the fullness thereof they shall be cut off.
120.3: Therefore, Lot went forth at that time and spake unto his sons-in-law and his married daughters and all who had gone forth with him from our camp, saying, Up, get you out of this place for on the morrow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will destroy this city.
120.4: But his words were as foolishness unto them and they mocked him.
120.5: And Lot returned unto his house in sorrow.

121.1: When morning came, the men of Elohim hastened Lot saying, Arise, take your wives and your daughters who are here with you in the house and depart now lest you be consumed by the wrath of Elohim which shall be visited upon the iniquities of Seḏom.
121.2: And while they were preparing to depart, Lot’s heart being full of sorrow at leaving his daughters and his daughters’ children to be destroyed, the men of Elohim took him by the hand with his wives and his daughters, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had mercy upon Lot because of his integrity, because he had not bowed down to false mighty ones nor entered into the abominations of Seḏom.
121.3: And Lot thought to dwell in Tso’ar; wherefore, he hastened there, but his wife Ado turned back unto the city of Seḏom.
121.4: Ado was the daughter of Ĕli, the son of Eli’ezer, which Ĕli had accompanied Lot to Seḏom.
121.5: And Ado thought upon her parents and her daughters who remained in the city, her heart was pained within her and she turned back to them and was lost.
121.6: But Lot entered with the rest of his family into Tso’ar and was there when the cities of the plains were overthrown.

122.1: Then the three qodesh men of Elohim came to me, Aḇraham, where I was fasting and praying nigh unto Seḏom, and they lifted me up into the shamayim and taught me the ordinances, the key words, and the signs by which I might call down fire and brimstone upon the cities.
122.2: And I did as I was commanded by the messengers of Elohim and the cities were destroyed.
122.3: And when I saw the destruction of the land, my heart was sorrowful, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said unto me, I have had mercy upon Lot and have sent him out of the city that he was not destroyed, for he was the only righteous man in all the cities.

123.1: And when the destruction was over, Lot feared to continue dwelling in Tso’ar, lest it also should be destroyed.
123.2: Wherefore, he took his family and went unto the cave of Aḏullam and dwelt there.
123.3: And the firstborn said to the younger, Our father is old, and there is no man on the earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth. Come, let us make our father drink wine, and let us lie with him, that we may preserve seed from our father.
123.4: So they made their father drink wine that night, and the firstborn went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she rose. And the next night they made him drink wine again, and the younger lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down or when she rose. Thus both daughters of Lot conceived by their father.
123.5: And the first-born bare a son and called his name Mo’aḇ.
123.6: And the younger also bare a son and she called his name Ben-Ammi.
123.7: And Lot dwelt in the cave for five years and after that he took his wives and his daughters and his sons whom his daughters had borne unto him and dwelt on the other side of Yardĕn.
123.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ him and prospered him and he dwelt in safety.

124.1: After the destruction of the cities of the plains, I, Aḇraham, journeyed to the south to the land of Gerar.
124.2: Now the meleḵ of the land of Gerar was Aḇimeleḵ, and he was one who worshipped the Most High Elohim and he was just and upright in all his ways.
124.3: And Aḇimeleḵ had entered the Qodesh Order of Elohim and was a kohĕn and a meleḵ after the Order of the Most High Elohim and had received the rites and ordinances of the Besorah.
124.4: As a youth he had dwelt with me in the city of Shalom and he was as a brother unto me and we shared all things.
124.5: When Sarah and I went in to Aḇimeleḵ to commune with him, the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon Aḇimeleḵ and he baraḵ Sarah in great outpourings after the Order of the Ancients and anointed her that she might bear qodesh seed and we rejoiced in the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to Sarah through the three qodesh men from the City of Ḥanoḵ and through His servant Aḇimeleḵ.
124.6: And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon me also and I baraḵ her and anointed her that the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 might fall upon her in a greater outpouring to the qodeshah of herself and her seed.
124.7: And we rejoiced together for three nights and two days and worshipped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim and were filled with joy and peace in the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 unto us.
124.8: And we were magnified in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

125.1: The next night, after Sarah and I had returned to our camp, Aḇimeleḵ was seated upon his throne praying when a sleep from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon him and he slept there all that night.
125.2: And while he slept, he dreamed a dream in which a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with a drawn sword in his hand came and stood above him.
125.3: And Aḇimeleḵ was frightened at the messenger, but the messenger said to him, Fear not, for because you have faithfully entered into the rites and ordinances of My Besorah and have walked a qodesh walk before Me and did uphold Shĕm and Aḇraham after him in the work which I have called them to do in maintaining My qodesh order in the earth, behold, I am sent to stand by your side and shall protect you against all the power of the adversary.
125.4: For your sins are forgiven you and your exaltation is sure and you shall dwell forever in the presence of Your Elohim.
125.5: So saying, the messenger departed from the vision of Aḇimeleḵ, but he felt His presence near him from that time forth and the adversary thereafter exercised no power over him.

126.1: We had dwelt in Gerar nine months when the three qodesh men of Elohim again visited us and Sarah gave birth to a son.
126.2: And on the eighth day he was circumcised according to the commandment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to me and I called his name Yitsḥaq. The child grew and when he was three years old he was weaned and I made a great feast on the day he was weaned.
126.3: And Malkitseḏeq, meleḵ of Shalom, with Ĕḇer his heir and Aḇimeleḵ, meleḵ of Gerar with his son, Aḇimeleḵ, and Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim, father to Haḡar and Yishma’ĕl, and all the mighty princes of the land came to the feast which I prepared, for these were the men whom I loved, with my brethren Aneram, Eshkol, and Mamrĕ.
126.4: My father, Teraḥ, also, and my brother, Naḥor, came unto the feast having heard that Sarah had borne a son. And we all rejoiced before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for many days that my son Yitsḥaq had reached the age of weaning from his mother.
126.5: And from that time forth Sarah and I introduced the lad into the Mishkan and began to instruct him in the mysteries of reverence that he might be prepared in his youth to enter into the Most Qodesh Place and be instructed there.
126.6: For Shĕm had instructed me in the city of Shalom that children should be instructed in the Hĕyḵal from the age of weaning which is three years old, that they should be instructed in the Most Qodesh Place from the age of puberty which is twelve years old, and that they should be endowed with power from on high from the age of maturity, which is fourteen years.
126.7: But inasmuch as I had not journeyed unto the city of Shalom until I was ten years old, I was prepared for the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s House in only a few years.

127.1: My son Yishma’ĕl, I did not introduce into 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s House in his childhood because he was not spiritual in his nature, but he was a hunter, proficient in the use of the bow and other instruments of death.
127.2: Nevertheless, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with Yishma’ĕl and baraḵ him for my sake in all to which he put his hand.
127.3: When Yitsḥaq was five years old, he was sitting with Yishma’ĕl at the door of Haḡar’s tent where Yishma’ĕl was sharpening his arrows, for Yishma’ĕl was sixteen years old at this time.
127.4: As they sat at the door of Haḡar’s tent, Yitsḥaq picked up one of Yishma’ĕl’s arrows and broke it.
127.5: Seeing this, Yishma’ĕl grew angry and taking another arrow, he fitted it to his bow intending to slay Yitsḥaq, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 touched his heart so that he did not slay him.
127.6: But Sarah saw this thing which Yishma’ĕl had intended to do to Yitsḥaq and she was grieved at it.
127.7: That night when I entered the tent of Sarah, she said to me, Let Haḡar and her son be sent to dwell apart, for this day did Yishma’ĕl seek to slay Yitsḥaq.
127.8: Now these words caused me great sorrow for I did not desire to see my family divided.
127.9: But that night a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came unto me in a dream, saying, Hearken unto the words of Sarah, your wife, and let Haḡar and her son Yishma’ĕl dwell apart lest harm come upon your son Yitsḥaq who shall be you heir.

128.1: Therefore, I arose early in the morning and took Haḡar and my son Yishma’ĕl into the deserts of Araḇia where dwelt a people who were friendly to me.
128.2: And there I built with Yishma’ĕl a Hĕyḵal to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim that his seed might always be kept in remembrance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
128.3: And Haḡar and Yishma’ĕl dwelt among the people of the desert and were content, and Yishma’ĕl was a mighty hunter with the bow among them.
128.4: And every year at a certain time I went and dwelt with my wife, Haḡar, and with my son, Yishma’ĕl.
128.5: And when Yishma’ĕl was twenty years of age, his mother asked my consent to take him to the house of her father in Mitsrayim, for she longed to see her family again.
128.6: Wherefore, I gave them my beraḵah and they departed into the land of Mitsrayim where they remained one year.
128.7: And while they were in Mitsrayim, Yishma’ĕl took to wife Meriḇah, daughter of Phanes, son of Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim.
128.8: And after he had taken Meriḇah to wife, they remained in the land of Mitsrayim yet ten years and Meriḇah bare unto Yishma’ĕl four sons and two daughters.
128.9: After this time, Yishma’ĕl took his mother and his wife and his children and returned to the deserts of Araḇia.
128.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ Yishma’ĕl for my sake and increased him in flocks and in herds and in good things.

129.1: When Yishma’ĕl had returned from the land of Mitsrayim, I went as was my custom to stay with my wife Haḡar and my son Yishma’ĕl.
129.2: And when Yishma’ĕl was away hunting, his wife Meriḇah spake disrespectfully to me and complained of my being in their tents.
129.3: Moreover, she abused her children and when I chastised her for this thing, she rose up in anger against me.
129.4: My wife Haḡar saw all these things, and when her son Yishma’ĕl had returned from the hunt, she complained unto him of the actions of Meriḇah toward me.
129.5: And Yishma’ĕl came to me and said, My father, what shall I do with such a wife who abused my father and my children and speak evil of me, for she had spoken against her husband Yishma’ĕl, also.
129.6: And I said to him, Such a one is not fit to be your wife nor the mother of your children nor to dwell in your tents; wherefore, give her a bill of divorcement and send her back to the home of her father in shame and find another more worthy than she to be your wife and the mother of these children.
129.7: So Yishma’ĕl gave unto Meriḇah a bill of divorcement and sent her back to her father Phanes in the land Mitsrayim and his mother Haḡar raised his children until he took another wife.

13.1: While Na’amah was yet a child, great consternation fell upon the seed of Qayin, for Iraḏ the son of Ḥanoḵ, the son of Qayin, had become a member of the secret combination and was privy to all it secrets until one night when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to him in a dream saying, Iraḏ, you have done evil instead of good and have followed after ha’Satan rather than Elohim; wherefore, I shall destroy you and your house when I send in the floods upon the earth.
13.2: But Iraḏ was pricked in his heart and pled with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to show mercy and preserve his seed through the great flood.
13.3: Seeing that his penitence was true, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, Iraḏ, if you will repent and reveal the evils of the secret combination to the sons of Shĕth, I will have mercy upon you and I will join your seed to the seed of Shĕth that it may be preserved through the great flood.
13.4: Wherefore, Iraḏ went forth and began to reveal the secrets of the sons of Qayin unto the sons of Shĕth.
13.5: Lemeḵ, being Master Mahan at that time, found Iraḏ sitting in his garden with Yoram, the young son of Iraḏ, and slew him.
13.6: Thus Lemeḵ slew Iraḏ for the sake of the oath of the secret combination and he slew Iraḏ’s son with him.
13.7: But Tuḇal-Qayin, the son of Lemeḵ, had followed him and viewed his evil deed which he had committed and he revealed it to his mother Tsillah and she to her sister Aḏah.
13.8: Wherefore, Aḏah and Tsillah confronted Lemeḵ with his evil and cursed him in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for having slain Iraḏ who had repented of his wickedness from among the sons of men.
13.9: And Lemeḵ said to his wives Aḏah and Tsillah, Hear my voice, ye wives of Lemeḵ; hearken to my speech, for I have slain a man to my wounding and a young man to my hurt.
13.10: If Qayin shall be avenged seven-fold, truly Lemeḵ shall be seventy and seven-fold.
13.11: Lemeḵ’s wives, therefore, feared to confront him further, but Lemeḵ did not repent of his evil deeds and finding his son Tuḇal-Qayin at prayer, he slew him for having revealed his murders.
13.12: When Aḏah and Tsillah, the wives of Lemeḵ, learned of this, they took their remaining sons and daughters and went unto their father Kena’an’s city and revealed the remainder of the secrets of this evil combination among the sons of Aḏam.
13.13: Thus did Na’amah come to dwell among the sons of Aḏam and she grew up before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in righteousness and was known for her tender care toward the sick and the unfortunate.
13.14: Nevertheless, she had no husband because she was of the forbidden race.

130.1: The next year Yishma’ĕl came to my camp and when he had kissed me and we had eaten together, he said to me, My father, according to your instructions I did give to my wife Meriḇah a bill of divorcement and sent her back to the home of her father in shame.
130.2: Now, therefore, I come to you to seek your counsel concerning obtaining another in her place.
130.3: Now, it pleased me that my son Yishma’ĕl had come to me regarding choosing a wife.
130.4: Therefore, I sought among the women of my camp and found two who were desirous of being wife to Yishma’ĕl, even Zola, the daughter of my wife Peleliah and Naiomi, the daughter Qemu’ĕl, the son of Qish, who had been among the believers who met in the room of my mother in the city of Ur.
130.5: And I was pleased to give them to my son Yishma’ĕl because he had come to me for counsel and because he had begun to magnify his kehunnah for he did worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim and sought to overcome his weaknesses.
130.6: And Yishma’ĕl and his family dwelt with me a long time in Gerar and after that, when I moved my camp to Be’ĕrsheḇa, which is by Ḥeḇron.

131.1: And Sarah and I continued to teach our son Yitsḥaq and instruct him in the ways of the ancients that he might be initiated into the Qodesh Order of Elohim and receive the bireḵoth of eternal lives.
131.2: And Yitsḥaq did know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with him and did baraḵ him greatly because he was full of faith and love and did good to all he met.

132.1: When Yitsḥaq was thirty-seven years old, he was one day talking with his brother Yishma’ĕl.
132.2: And Yishma’ĕl was boasting of his righteousness, saying, I was thirteen years old when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spake to my father to circumcise us, and from that time I have consecrated my being to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and kept His Commandments as they have come to me from my father.
132.3: But Yitsḥaq answered him saying, Why do you boast in your righteousness, for none of us are without sin and all mankind is as nothing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
132.4: And we must be prepared to be offered upon the altar as a sacrifice to our Elohim with joy that we can esteem Him before our calling and election is made sure.

133.1: This saying of Yitsḥaq’s pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 visited me, saying, your son Yitsḥaq have I seen and his heart is right before me and he is clean and pure, an acceptable sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
133.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 touched the eyes of my understanding that they were opened and I saw the sons of Elohim gathered in council with the Father and Hĕlĕl, also was among them.
133.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Hĕlĕl, Surely you have been abroad in the earth trying the hearts of men.
133.4: Whom have you found standing in his integrity who should be further tried to know whether he be yours or mine?
133.5: Hĕlĕl replied, Have you considered Aḇraham and Sarah and Yitsḥaq? For I am unable to lead them into sin in whatever matter I place before them.
133.6: They are united in perfect bonds of love and purity and even Aḇraham has united all his family again which was divided.
133.7: Surely they should be tried to know whether they are faithful only in their prosperity or whether they will be faithful also in adversity.
133.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Hĕlĕl, Were I to say to Aḇraham, Bring up Yitsḥaq your son to the high place and offer him as a burnt offering to me, he would not withhold him from me nor would Yitsḥaq refuse to be offered.
133.9: And Hĕlĕl answered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Speak now to Aḇraham as you have said and we shall see whether his heart is perfect with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 or whether his end shall be in my reign.

134.1: With these words, the vision was closed to my mind and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, Aḇraham, take now your son Yitsḥaq whom you love and go to the land of Moriyah and offer him there for a burnt offering upon the mountain upon which you shall see the splendor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 resting as a cloud.
134.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 departed from me and left me to consider these things.

135.1: Now Sarah’s heart was knit to Yitsḥaq’s insomuch that she did keep him by her side whenever possible and he did sleep upon her bed at night.
135.2: Wherefore, I thought, How shall I separate Yitsḥaq from his mother Sarah for such a journey lest her heart be grieved and she die in her grief?
135.3: So I went in to Sarah and comforted her and afterwards I said to her, Our son Yitsḥaq we have taught these many years and I feel now that I should take him unto Shĕm and Ĕḇer, his son, where he can be instructed by the ancient ones in the mysteries of the ancients that he may become a perfect servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.
135.4: Sarah replied, You have spoken well, my master. Go now and do all as you have said, only let the lad remain not too long apart from me for my being is bound to his being with a perfect love from Elohim.
135.5: And I answered Sarah saying, My daughter, let us pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim that we may yield to His Will in all things and that all things will work together for our good.

136.1: And Yitsḥaq slept with us that night and Sarah kissed and embraced him and instructed him until morning.
136.2: And she said to him, O my son, how can my being separate itself from you?
136.3: And she still kissed and embraced him until the time of preparation had come.
136.4: Then Sarah took a beautiful and costly robe from among those which Aḇimeleḵ had given her, for Aḇimeleḵ had loved Sarah greatly and had given her many precious things, but his love toward her was pure in the sight of Elohim and according to the laws of the shamayim.
136.5: With this robe which had never been worn, Sarah clothed Yitsḥaq and put a turban upon his head in which she wrapped a precious stone.
136.6: And she said unto him, Even this stone are you precious to me, my son.
136.7: Nevertheless, I would have you so conduct your life that when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall come to gather up his jewels, you will be among the number.

137.1: Thus, taking provisions for our journey, we started out and Sarah and others of our people accompanied us upon the road.
137.2: And when the time of parting had arrived, Sarah wept bitterly and I also wept with her as did Yitsḥaq our son and those who accompanied us.
137.3: And Sarah caught hold of Yitsḥaq and held him in her arms and embraced him and kissed him and wept over him and Sarah said to him, Who knows if after this day I shall ever see you again?
137.4: Nevertheless, our hope is in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in whom is life.
137.5: Therefore, if I see you not again in this veil of tears, yet surely we shall again embrace before the throne of Elohim.
137.6: Elohim baraḵ you, my son, and keep you secure in His Ways and I will be close to you all your days.
137.7: So saying, Sarah kissed Yitsḥaq again and turned back to the camp with all who had accompanied us.

138.1: As we proceeded upon our journey, ha’Satan came to me in the form of an aged man, humble and contrite, who said to me, How can you think to do so to your son?
138.2: Did not Elohim give you this son by a qodesh conception after the Order of the Ancients and do you think so little of this precious gift that you will take his life as you would slaughter a dumb beast and cut off your only hope of a royal posterity in the earth?
138.3: What evil has he done to you that you should do this thing?
138.4: Do you not understand that this thing cannot be from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
138.5: Behold 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 delights not in human sacrifice.
138.6: Did He not smite the priest of Nimroḏ for seeking to take your life in like manner?
138.7: Surely you should repent of this your purpose and return your son to the bed of his mother, Sarah.
138.8: But I knew that this was the word of ha’Satan seeking to prevent my obeying the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; wherefore, I commanded him to depart by the authority of the qodesh kehunnah in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and he departed from me in haste.

139.1: A short time later, ha’Satan came again, appearing to Yitsḥaq in the form of a handsome and pleasing young man.
139.2: And he said unto Yitsḥaq, Do you not understand that your old father in his foolishness is bringing you to be slain today for no purpose?
139.3: Now therefore, my brother, go not with him for it is the foolishness of his old age that does this.
139.4: Therefore, let not your precious life and your beautiful body be lost from the earth in such a manner, but come with me and I will introduce you to the pleasures of the earth and you shall take pleasure therein all your days.
139.5: When Yitsḥaq heard this, he said to me, My father, surely this is ha’Satan come to dissuade me from obeying the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for does he appear and thus does he say to me.
139.6: Wherefore, my father, rebuke him in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that he shall cease from troubling me for I know that you are a servant of the Most High Elohim and that it is to fulfill the Will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that we are come to this place.
139.7: Wherefore, I, Aḇraham, rebuked ha’Satan in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Noaḥ and of Shĕm, and he departed from us in fear.

14.1: When the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came unto Noaḥ, saying, Take for yourself Na’amah, the daughter of Lemeḵ who dwells here in the city of your fathers, for she has been faithful to My Besorah, wherefore, I shall preserve through her the seed of Qayin through the flood, Noaḥ went to his father, Methushelaḥ.
14.2: Methushelaḥ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and returned this word to his son Lemeḵ: Truely, this what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, My handmaiden Na’amah have I given to My son Noaḥ that the seed of Qayin might be preserved through the great flood which I will send upon the earth.
14.3: Wherefore, let not My son Noaḥ fear to take her to wife, for in so doing he shall be baruḵ for through him will come all nations.
14.4: Wherefore, say to him, Noaḥ, My son, I have looked upon the evils of the sons of men which have come up before Me, for they have corrupted the whole earth except only this city in which you dwell.
14.5: Therefore, I will send in the floods upon the earth but you and your seed will I preserve through the flood, for I will send My messengers to instruct you in the building of an ark where you shall be saved.
14.6: Behold, I shall establish your seed before Me forever and I will spread them abroad over the earth as numerous as the sand upon the seashore.
14.7: Your seed shall not cease as long as the earth shall stand but through you and your kehunnah which will be preserved in your seed shall all nations be baruḵ.

140.1: As we continued on our journey, we entered a narrow ravine with high walls.
140.2: When we were in the midst of it, we heard a mighty rumbling and the earth shook beneath our feet.
140.3: Looking back, we saw a great wall of water coming down upon us bearing trees and boulders in a mighty flood.
140.4: My heart was moved within me for my son Yitsḥaq and he sought also to protect me, but, raising my hands to the shamayim I called upon the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard me out of the shamayim and stopped the flood until we had ascended from the ravine.
140.5: Thus did ha’Satan seek to destroy us that we might not offer an acceptable sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim but the power of our Elohim is mightier than that of ha’Satan; wherefore, ha’Satan can do no harm to the children of men except 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim allow him to do it.
140.6: Therefore, do all things, whether they be good or evil, work together for the good of the qodeshim of Elohim who serve Him and keep His Commandments.

141.1: And on the third day, we saw the place afar off which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had appointed for the sacrifice of my beloved son Yitsḥaq.
141.2: And I knew the place because the splendor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was there as a pillar of fire and a radiant cloud.
141.3: And when I saw the place, I said to my son Yitsḥaq, My son, do you see that upon the mountain?
141.4: And Yitsḥaq replied, yea, my father, for the splendor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rests upon it as a pillar of fire and a splendid cloud.
141.5: Then I rejoiced that my son was found worthy to see this sign also and we bowed down there and worshipped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.

142.1: As we approached the mountain, Yitsḥaq said to me, My father, we have with us the fire and the wood, but we have no lamb to serve as a burnt offering unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
142.2: Explain now to me the mystery hidden in this thing that I may be obedient to all which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim requires of me.
142.3: Then I rejoiced, for I knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had revealed in the heart of my son Yitsḥaq that which we must do.
142.4: Therefore I said to him, Yitsḥaq, my son, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen you to be a perfect burnt offering to Him instead of the lamb.
142.5: And this thing is a type of Ruaḥoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is our first Father and His Only Begotten Bĕn who is the Lamb slain from before the foundation to the earth.
142.6: For surely Elohim will offer His only Bĕn as a sacrifice upon the stake to atone for our sins and for the sins of all mankind, that all men might be redeemed from the power of death and be brought to stand before the judgement bar of the great 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to be judged according to their works, that every man might receive a righteous and just judgment and that mercy might have claim upon the penitent, the price of their sins having been paid by the Bĕn of Elohim.
142.7: Yea, surely, my son, we have been chosen to represent the Father and the Bĕn in this thing, and though I grieve to think of losing you, my beloved, yet I rejoice that we are honored thus to represent Elohim.

143.1: And Yitsḥaq said to me, I will do all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded you, my father, with joy in my heart that I am chosen to represent the Bĕn of Elohim in this sacrifice, and I have this hope in me, that if we are faithful to all the Commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, I shall yet stand in the flesh with you and my mother before the throne of the Ancient of Days and receive from Him the promise of exaltation and eternal lives.
143.2: When I heard this answer, I rejoiced in my son Yitsḥaq whose heart was pure and upright before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
143.3: But the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 constrained me to test him further, and I said to him, Have you any thoughts or feelings which would prevent your being offered as a perfect sacrifice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
143.4: For if you do in any way doubt the efficacy of this sacrifice, which is in the similitude of the sacrifice of the Only Begotten of the Father which is full of favor and truth, it is not meet that you should be offered as a sacrifice before our Elohim.
143.5: But Yitsḥaq answered me saying, O my father, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives and as you live as a qodesh man of Elohim, I know that you are a servant of the Most High Elohim and that you do hold the keys of the fathers.
143.6: You have never asked me to do anything which was not of Elohim but you have taught me by precept and example to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in every act of my life.
143.7: Shall I then shrink from being offered by you as a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim?
143.8: No, but I shall rejoice forever to have been so honored.
143.9: Baruḵ is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 you Elohim who has this day chosen me to be sacrificed as a burnt offering before Him.

144.1: Thus we came unto the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had appointed for the offering of my son, rejoicing in the splendor of our Elohim.
144.2: Yet I did weep at the thought of losing my beloved son Yitsḥaq and at the knowledge of the pain this would bring to his mother Sarah, for their beings were united as one.
144.3: Nevertheless, my heart rejoiced that I was chosen with my son for this qodesh ordinance that we might thereby magnify the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

145.1: After kneeling in prayer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, Yitsḥaq and I constructed an altar before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and I laid the wood in order upon the altar which we had built.
145.2: And Yitsḥaq lay upon the altar and I bound him there and he said to me, Bind me securely lest I move beneath the force of the knife and profane the offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
145.3: So I bound him securely that he could not move upon the altar.
145.4: And I wept as I prepared my son for the sacrifice and Yitsḥaq wept with me, yet our hearts rejoiced to have been found worthy of this great beraḵah.

146.1: When all was prepared, I picked up the knife, kissed my son Yitsḥaq, and prepared to offer him as a sacrifice unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim.
146.2: But the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came unto me saying, Aḇraham, slay not your son, for I have tested you in this manner that I might know that your hearts are perfect before Me.
146.3: Now I know that you fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in that you have not withheld your heir from My altar and he has willingly lain thereon to be a sacrifice of a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
146.4: Therefore, lift up your eyes and behold the ram that was chosen from the beginning to stand in the place of your son Yitsḥaq as a burnt offering before Me.
146.5: And I looked up and saw a ram caught by his horns in a thicket.
146.6: For as the ram had advanced to the sacrifice, ha’Satan had caught him in the thicket that he might not be offered in Yitsḥaq’s stead.
146.7: But I went and freed him from the thicket and releasing my son Yitsḥaq, I placed the ram upon the altar and offered him in Yitsḥaq’s place, that his blood might be considered as the blood of Yitsḥaq before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
146.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 accepted the sacrifice of the ram as if it had been Yitsḥaq and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to us and baraḵ me and my seed on that day.

147.1: When all things were finished, Yitsḥaq and I returned to our camp rejoicing in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.
147.2: But when we reached the place we found that Sarah was not there, for the agents of ha’Satan had come to her saying, Behold, do you not understand that Aḇraham goes to offer your son Yitsḥaq as a burnt offering unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim?
147.3: Surely he does this because he is jealous of your love for your son Yitsḥaq.
147.4: Go, therefore, and stop this thing lest he to whom your heart is knitted be destroyed from off the face of the earth.

148.1: But Sarah said, Surely the heart of my master Aḇraham is right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim for he walks before Him in all His Ways.
148.2: Nevertheless, shall my son Yitsḥaq be offered as a burnt offering and I not be there to weep over him and strengthen him and pray for him that he be an acceptable offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Aḇraham?
148.3: No, but I shall go to him.
148.4: And Sarah departed with her menservants and her maidservants and went as far as Ḥeḇron but found us not.
148.5: Therefore, Sarah rested in Ḥeḇron and sent her young men to find us, who searched all the land round about and even in the city of Shalom but found us not.
148.6: Then Sarah prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saying, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Aḇraham, surely I know that all things are in your hand, and I do not fear for my son Yitsḥaq for I know that my husband Aḇraham is a kohĕn ha’gadol after Your qodesh order.
148.7: Nevertheless, it is my desire to be with my son at this qodesh hour that I might share his joy and his sorrow before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.

149.1: Then the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Sarah saying, Surely I have accepted the offering of Yitsḥaq and have provided a ram prepared before the foundation of the earth that was laid to be offered in his place; wherefore, your son lives and is with his father Aḇraham and even now searches for you.
149.2: When Sarah heard these words, her heart was filled with joy so that she could not contain it and her spirit was lifted up to see the Paradise of Elohim and she exclaimed, Behold, I have seen my Redeemer and it suffices me, and she gave up the ghost.
149.3: Thus did Sarah die in Ḥeḇron being one hundred and twenty-seven years old and she died having seen her Redeemer and having received from Him the promise of eternal life.

15.1: When Lemeḵ returned this word to his son, Noaḥ rejoiced and praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saying, I give thanks to You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for You have been to me a strong wall against all that would seek my destruction.
15.2: Yea, You have promised to shelter me from the disasters which are coming upon the earth, that the floods shall not come in upon me to destroy my seed from the earth.
15.3: You have set my foot upon a rock that the sons of men shall not prevail against me.
15.4: Yea, I will walk in the way of the Ancients; in the paths which You have appointed will I spend my days for You are my Shield and my Deliverer and in You will I trust all the days on my life. Amĕn.

150.1: Then was word brought to us, that Sarah was gone to Ḥeḇron, wherefore we journeyed there and found that Sarah had died.
150.2: But having inquired after the manner of her death, we rejoiced that she went with the promise of exaltation and that she died knowing of Yitsḥaq’s deliverance and his acceptance with Elohim.
150.3: Then we took Sarah to a cave which I purchased of Ephron the Ḥittite for that purpose and we buried her there and we wept over her, yet we rejoiced in her righteousness before Elohim.
150.4: And all the people of the land came to honor Sarah with Pharaoh who came from Mitsrayim and Aḇimeleḵ from Gerar and many others who honored and loved Sarah.
150.5: For she was truly a handmaiden of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and ministered to many in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in love and charity and was greatly loved by all for her kindness meekness and her great wisdom in reverence.

151.1: Thus, I, Aḇraham, began to be old having seen one hundred and thirty-seven years.
151.2: Wherefore, I write this record of my life that others might benefit from the workings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim with me.
151.3: And I bear this witness that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives and reigns in the shamayim, and He is the Most High Elohim over all the earth.
151.4: He has led me since first He appeared to me in a dream when I was three years of age, even to this time when I am old and bowed down with years.
151.5: He has done only good to me and not evil all the days of my life.
151.6: Surely I will love Him and serve Him forever and ever and will magnify His Name on high before all people. Amĕn.

152.1: After Sarah’s death, I sent my son Yitsḥaq unto Shĕm and Ĕḇer to learn more perfectly the ways of the ancients and he remained there three years before returning to my camp.

153.1: In the one hundred thirty-eighth year of my life, my brother Aḇimeleḵ, meleḵ of Gerar, died being one hundred and ninety-three years of age.
153.2: Wherefore, I took my people and journeyed to Gerar where we mourned over Aḇimeleḵ for he was a good and qodesh man who walked in perfectness before his Elohim and had made his calling and his election sure.
153.3: Therefore, we rejoiced in knowing of his end.
153.4: Nevertheless, we sorrowed to be parted from him, but I knew that I should soon go to him, which knowledge comforted my heart.
153.5: And his son Aḇimeleḵ was chosen to reign in his stead.

154.1: The following year Lot, my brother’s son, died being one hundred and forty years old.
154.2: He, too, was a just man and accepted of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, although he did not walk in all the ways of the ancients, for he had coveted his own property and separated from the community of Elohim, therefore he must receive a just reward.
154.3: Nevertheless, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loved him because he maintained his integrity, even in the midst of wicked Seḏom, wherefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved him and those of his household who would be saved from destruction, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made of him also a mighty people.

155.1: Now, when my son Yitsḥaq was about to return to me from the city of Shalom, the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me saying, Behold, in the city of Ḥaran dwells Bethu’ĕl the son of your brother Naḥor who is dead.
155.2: Unto Bethu’ĕl has been born Riḇqah, who at this time is ten years of age.
155.3: Send now and fetch her as a wife to your son Yitsḥaq, for this have I appointed that she shall bear to him the chosen seed.

156.1: So I called to me Eli’ezer, my trusted companion who had been with me since we had come out of the city of Shalom, and I said to him, Put now your hand under my thigh and swear to me before the Most High Elohim that you shall go unto the city of Ḥaran and bring from there Riḇqah, daughter of Bethu’ĕl son of Naḥor my brother to be a wife to my son Yitsḥaq according to the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but if the maiden refuse to come with you, you shall be free of this oath.
156.2: So Eli’ezer swore before the Most High Elohim and departed from me in peace.
156.3: He also pursued his journey to Ḥaran and found Riḇqah, even as I had said, and returned with her after the return of my son Yitsḥaq from the city of Shalom.
156.4: Thus Yitsḥaq took Riḇqah to wife when he was forty years old, he having four other wives; but Riḇqah he took to wife in the tent of Sarah.
156.5: And Riḇqah bare no children; wherefore I knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 should work a marvelous work in her even as in Sarah before her.
156.6: Therefore, my heart rejoiced in Riḇqah, the wife of my son Yitsḥaq, for she was pure and virtuous like to Sarah my beloved who had preceded me into the rest of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

157.1: This same year I took to wife Qeturah, the daughter of my old friend Aḇimeleḵ meleḵ of Gerar who was dead.
157.2: Qeturah bare me six sons so that in all I received of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 eight sons and three hundred and twenty-eight daughters, being in all three hundred and thirty-six beings.
157.3: Thus did 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 increase me greatly besides the many sons who were adopted to me.
157.4: And thus I increased continually before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

158.1: After nine years my son Yitsḥaq brought to me his wife Riḇqah for she was yet barren.
158.2: And she said to me, My father, surely I know that my mother Sarah was barren for many years before she bare Yitsḥaq to you.
158.3: Wherefore, pray for me, that I, like Sarah, may conceive.
158.4: Therefore, I prayed over my daughter Riḇqah, and I said to Yitsḥaq, Your mother Sarah bare you after she received a beraḵah from my brother Aḇimeleḵ meleḵ of Gerar.
158.5: Aḇimeleḵ, son of Aḇimeleḵ, reign now in the place of his father in Gerar, and he, too, is a mighty man of Elohim.
158.6: Go you in unto him that he may baraḵ Riḇqah and she shall conceive and bear to you two sons and the younger shall rule over the elder, but in the elder shall the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 also be fulfilled for through him shall I slay wicked Nimroḏ even as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 foretold at my birth.
158.7: So Yitsḥaq took Riḇqah and went to Gerar, to Aḇimeleḵ, son of Aḇimeleḵ, who baraḵ her after the Order of the Ancients, and she conceived and bare to Yitsḥaq two sons, even as I had said.
158.8: And on the eighth day, Yitsḥaq brought the last to me to be named and the elder I called Ĕsaw, for he was covered with hair and I said, Surely he shall be a mighty hunter before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
158.9: But the second I called Ya’aqoḇ, for I said, Surely the elder shall serve the younger.

159.1: When my youngest son Shuwaḥ, whom Qeturah had borne me - for she bare Zimran, Yoqshan, Miḏyan, Meḏan, Yishbaq and Shuwaḥ - was fifteen years of age, I called all of my sons unto me and instructed them in the Ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and baraḵ them and gave unto each wives and a goodly inheritance of property according to the instructions of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and sent them away to inherit lands which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had prepared for them.
159.2: Then I rested in peace knowing that I had done all the will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and that soon I should be gathered to my fathers to be with Sarah and the righteous in the Paradise of Elohim.

16.1: Thus did Noaḥ take to wife Na’amah, the daughter of Tsillah, the wife of Lemeḵ of the seed of Qayin, and she bare him a son whom he named Ḥam, and this was the curse preserved in the land through the great flood.
16.2: For when the patience of Elohim was ended in which He did grant a space of time for repentance to the sons of men, the floods came in upon the earth and destroyed all flesh from off the face of the earth save eight beings only, for Noaḥ and his youngest wife Aḏah, and his three sons Shĕm, Yepheth, and Ḥam and one of each of their wives were preserved in the ark which the messengers had instructed Noaḥ in building.
16.3: The remainder of the righteous had died or been caught up into Ḥanoḵ’s city prior to the time of the flood, and these eight were saved.

160.1: Behold, I am Yitsḥaq, the son of Aḇraham, and I finish my father’s record.
160.2: For when the end of my father’s sojourn among men had come, he called me to him and said, My son, according to the Commandment of Elohim to you, I have appointed you to be my heir that all the authority I possess should rest with you.
160.3: You know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is Elohim in the shamayim and earth and we serve only Him.
160.4: He has many times preserved me from destruction when the evil ones would have destroyed me, for I always place my trust in Him.
160.5: He brought me to this land and said to me, To your seed will I give all this land and they shall inherit it when they shall keep My Commandments, My Statutes and My Judgments that I have Commanded you and which I shall Command them.
160.6: Now therefore my son, hearken to My voice and keep the Commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, even as you have been instructed by me and by your mother Sarah and by Shĕm and Ĕḇer.
160.7: Depart not from the qodesh order of Elohim in any particular and remember always the mercies of our Elohim and His beraḵah will never depart from you.
160.8: Teach these things also to your children and your children’s children that they may receive the like bireḵoth with us for all those who obey the Torah of the fathers will be baruḵ with the fathers.

161.1: Then I covenanted with my father to do all things as he had said and to walk always in his ways.
161.2: And my father baraḵ me and my house and he took my son Ya’aqoḇ into his tent, he being fifteen years old at this time, and instructed him for seven days and nights in the ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
161.3: Thus did my father end his days and he died, being one hundred and seventy-five years of age.
161.4: And Yishma’ĕl and his other sons returned to me and we did bury our father with Sarah my mother and all the inhabitants of the land did mourn over him for he was a righteous man who did good to all.
161.5:
And truly this was his testimony, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is Elohim over all and those who serve Him shall inherit peace in this life and eternal joy in the life to come. Amĕn.
- Sarah and Aḇraham

17.1: Now when the flood had abated and the ark had come to rest upon the top of a mountain, Noaḥ and his family descended the mountain and after offering sacrifices unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and dedicating the land, they began to till the ground and raise all manner of crops.
17.2: And when the grape harvest was come in, Noaḥ made wine and drank of the new wine in his tent and his heart was made glad and he rejoiced before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the bounty which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had given him.
17.3: And it was upon the Feast of Shaḇuoth when Noaḥ drank of the new wine before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and lay down naked in his tent to sleep.
17.4: When Ḥam, the son of Noaḥ, entered the tent he saw his father sleeping naked upon his bed with the qodesh garments which had been given to Aḏam in the garden of Ĕḏen laying nearby.
17.5: Ḥam knew that he and his posterity could not bear the kehunnah because of the curse of Qayin which was upon them and knowing there was great power in the qodesh garments, he stole them from his father Noaḥ and hurried to his tents.
17.6: Rousing his family, Ḥam instructed them to strike their tents and led them away to the plain of Shin’ar where he dwelt and where Ḥam died.
17.7: Now Ḥam’s wife was named Zeptah and she was also of the seed of Qayin and they had a daughter named Zeptah.
17.8: This daughter, after the death of Ḥam, led a body of his people westward until they reached a body of water in the land of Zeptah, which is Mitsrayim, where they settled and as the waters receded from off the land, they spread out and built many cities and temples.

18.1: Before the death of Ḥam, the qodesh garments were given secretly by him to his son Kush.
18.2: Kush also kept them hidden and in his old age gave them unto his son Nimroḏ and when Nimroḏ was twenty years of age, he put on the garments and he derived great strength and power from them.
18.3: Moreover, Nimroḏ was instructed in all the secrets of the evil combination by his father.
18.4: Wherefore, Nimroḏ became a mighty man among the sons of men and established his reign and grew stronger and stronger in wickedness after the order of the secret combination which was from the beginning, for Nimroḏ spread his dominion over all mankind except those in the city of Shalom.

19.1: Shĕm ruled in the city of Shalom and he was called Malkitseḏeq, for he reigned as meleḵ under his father Noaḥ, and was a kohĕn of the Most High Elohim.
19.2: After the departure of Ḥam from the presence of his father Noaḥ, Shĕm and Yepheth dwelt together in peace under the benign rule of Noaḥ; but in time, conflict arose among them and Noaḥ led the seed of Shĕm to a new land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showed him where they built a city which they called Shalom, the City of Peace.
19.3: Noaḥ invested his son Shĕm with authority to reign as Prince of Peace, and Noaḥ devoted his days to instructing his people after the Order of the Ancients.
19.4: And his people dwelt in righteousness and worshipped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim and served Him.
19.5: They established the order of the shamayim among them and sought after the City of Ḥanoḵ and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came among them and ministered to them and those who sought for the gain of this world went out from among them, for they held all things common after the order of Ḥanoḵ and no man was above his neighbor.

2.1: I, Aḇraham, was born the son of Teraḥ who was Prime Minister to Nimroḏ who reigned in Ur of the Kasdim.
2.2: Now this Nimroḏ was a wicked man and an idolater and my father - Teraḥ - was led to follow after his abominations.
2.3: Moreover, Nimroḏ was a man of mighty power for he was Master Mahan and had in his hands the secrets of the ancients as they had come down from Qayin wherein he knew the words of power and the signs for using them and he had the qodesh garments which had been given unto Aḏam in the garden in which was great power.
2.4: All of this power did Nimroḏ use to get gain after the manner of the secret combination.
2.5: With his power he had set out to build a tower which would reach to the shamayim, even the city of my father Ḥanoḵ which had been taken up, that he, Nimroḏ, might depose Elohim from His throne for Elohim had taken up His abode among the people of Ḥanoḵ.
2.6: But Elohim frustrated the plans of Nimroḏ by confounding the language of him and his people that they could no longer remember the qodesh words and they scattered forth over the face of the earth.
2.7: At that time Nimroḏ came and established the city of Ur which is the City of Light, for he yet retained his determination to build a city to rival the city of Elohim that the light and power might center in him.
2.8: And through the ministration of ha’Satan he did receive again some of the words of power and did reorganize the secret combination among his people; but he had not power as at the first for the fullness of the pure language was not restored to him according to the decree of the Most High Elohim.
2.9: Now, in all the wickedness of Nimroḏ, my father stood by his side for he was deceived by the subtle cunning and power which Nimroḏ possessed.

20.1: Among those who went forth from the city of Shalom was Peleḡ, who traveled to the northwest and established a city after the order of his father Noaḥ, for Peleḡ was the son of Ĕḇer, the son of Shelaḥ, the son of Arpaḵshaḏ, the son of Shĕm; and his people sought after the order of the shamayim and obtained it for they were caught up like the City of Ḥanoḵ.
