20.2: But Seruḡ, the son of Re’u, the son of Peleḡ, followed not after the way of his fathers, for he sought after gain for himself; wherefore, he led those who were of a like mind with himself out from the City of Peleḡ and they journeyed even unto the land of Shin’ar and became confederate with Nimroḏ.
20.3: Under the direction of Nimroḏ, Seruḡ and his companions entered into the secret combination and became men of power and wealth in Nimroḏ’s reign.
20.4: In the land of Shin’ar, Seruḡ begat Naḥor, and Naḥor begat Teraḥ, my father.
20.5: And Teraḥ became great in the eyes of Nimroḏ, and Nimroḏ elevated him over all his people to stand at his right hand and advise him on all matters.

21.1: Now, my father Teraḥ took many wives and begat many children.
21.2: And when he was sixty-five years of age, he took to wife Amthelo, the daughter of Korneḇo, the son of Seruḡ, and she was a young woman of fifteen years.
21.3: And when Teraḥ was seventy years old, his wife Amthelo conceived and bare him a son whom he named Aḇram, which the interpretation is Exalted Father, for he said, Nimroḏ has raised me on high over all his host, wherefore, my seed shall reign as mighty ones forever.
21.4: Now this neḇuah he spake, not knowing that it was of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim.

22.1: On the night that I was born, there were great signs in the shamayim, and when Nimroḏ’s astrologers saw them, they were astonished and they spake evil of me to the meleḵ, saying that surely I should overthrow his reign.
22.2: Wherefore, they counseled the meleḵ to purchase me of my father that they might slay me and this frustrates the plans of Elohim.
22.3: Meleḵ Nimroḏ thereupon sent for my father, Teraḥ, and spake to him of the words of the astrologers and asked for his son in return for a great sum of gold and silver.
22.4: But the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 wrought upon my father that he was loathe to give me up to the meleḵ.
22.5: On the night that I was born, a son was also born to one of my father’s concubines and this child my father took to the meleḵ and the meleḵ slew him in my stead, for this had Elohim ordained that I might grow up to serve Him, the only wise and true Elohim, and strive to establish His order in the earth all my days.

23.1: This was my life saved by my father Teraḥ, and he took me with my mother, Amthelo, and my nurse, Eḏna, into a cave hidden in the mountains some distance from the city of Ur where he secreted us and visited us each month at the New Moon.
23.2: For my father informed the meleḵ that he went each month on the New Moon to a spot qodesh to his family deity.
23.3: For in the reign of Nimroḏ, each man worshipped mighty ones of his own make, mighty ones of wood and stone, each after the imagination of his own heart.
23.4: I dwelled in the cave with my mother, Amthelo, and my nurse, Eḏna, and knew no other man except my father, Teraḥ, and my elder brothers, Haran and Naḥor, who accompanied my father on his visits.

24.1: When I was three years of age, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 visited me in a dream of the night and he said to me, Aḇram.
24.2: And I said, Here am I.
24.3: And He said to me, Aḇram, I am the Elohim of your fathers Peleḡ and Shĕm and Noaḥ.
24.4: It is I who preserved your life when the wicked meleḵ Nimroḏ would have destroyed you, for I softened the heart of your father that he should hide you away.
24.5: This I did for I have a mighty work for you to do in establishing My order upon the earth, and, truly, I say to you, in the end, through you shall this wicked Nimroḏ be destroyed from off the face of the earth.
24.6: Behold, you shall remain in this cave with your mother and your nurse for seven years, and at the end of that time you shall depart and I will send My messenger to guide you to the city of you father Noaḥ where you shall be instructed in the way of ḥai.
24.7: And from that time forth 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 instructed me often in dreams of the night that my mind was opened to the Ways of His Reign.

25.1: When I was ten years of age, I departed from the cave by night while my mother and my nurse slept and the messenger of Elohim met me and led me to the city of Shalom where Noaḥ and his son Shĕm dwelt, and no man knew where I was.
25.2: And I dwelt with Noaḥ and Shĕm for thirty-nine years, being instructed in all the Ways of the Most High Elohim.
25.3: And finding great happiness and peace and rest therein, I sought for the bireḵoth of the Fathers and I received, under the direction of Noaḥ and Shĕm, those instructions whereby I might enter into the Order of the Ancients and I became a rightful heir and kohĕn ha’gadol, holding the right belonging to the Fathers. For I was ushered into the Assembly of the First-born and tasted the fruits of ḥai of the shamayim.

26.1: In my fiftieth year, Father Shĕm called me into his presence and instructed me to return to the house of my father, for there were many there now who were seeking after light and truth for they had seen the foolishness of worshipping mighty ones of wood and stone, but they knew not where to find the true Elohim.
26.2: And Father Shĕm baraḵ me saying, Baruḵ are you Aḇram of the Most High Elohim for He has looked upon you and found your heart right before Him.
26.3: For this cause, the Most High shall visit you and you shall stand at the head and be the father of a multitude, for many nations shall spring forth from your loins.
26.4: Behold, in your father’s house dwells a women to whom the promises belong, for she is a princess in the house of the Most High and shall reign as a queen over your posterity forever.
26.5: Seek after her and take her to wife for she will be the mother of the promised seed.
26.6: The bireḵoth of the Elohim of Noaḥ attend you, my son, as you journey on your way, from this time forth, you shall be a wanderer in the earth until your seed shall come to inherit this land by the power of Elohim and the sword of His might.
26.7: Be faithful always, preach the truth in soberness and be valiant in the cause of Elohim, and you shall be baruḵ forevermore. Amĕn.

27.1: With this beraḵah resting upon me, I gathered together my family, for I had taken seven wives in the city of Shalom who had borne me fifty daughters.
27.2: And although I had no sons of mine own flesh, yet I had adopted twelve sons of those who were faithful to the Order of the Ancients and foremost among these was Eli’ezer of Dammeseq who had come to the city of Shalom seeking after the bireḵoth of the Fathers and had remained as my son.
27.3: Him I appointed as steward over all I possessed for this journey, for he stood as my heir for I loved him as my son and brother.
27.4: But Father Shĕm said unto me, Eli’ezer is a good and righteous man and he shall be greatly baruḵ in time and in eternity, but he shall not be your heir, for another shall be your heir who shall come forth from the womb of your wife whom you shall take in the house of your father, for she is ordained to be the queen of queens and the mother of your heir.
27.5: Wherefore, as I have said, I gathered together my wives and my daughters and my adopted sons and their wives and children and I said unto them, Hear my words, beloved and hearken unto my speech, for I have been sent with a mission unto the house of my father in the land of Shin’ar to gather out the pure in heart who are seeking after the true Elohim.
27.6: Gather together all your goods and make tents in which to dwell and saddle your donkeys to travel upon for the Most High Elohim has declared that we shall be wanderers upon the earth from this time forth until our seed shall come in to inherit this land by the power of Elohim and the sword of His might.

28.1: Then we began our preparations and on the appointed day, all was in readiness for our departure.
28.2: And when father Shĕm came forth to baraḵ us, father Noaḥ came also with him.
28.3: Now father Noaḥ dwelt in the Hĕyḵal in the heart of the city of Shalom and seldom came out of the qodesh place, for I had never seen him without its qodesh precincts.
28.4: But he came forth at this time and lifted up his hands and baraḵ us in the name of the Most High Elohim and we departed from his house.

29.1: We journeyed slowly for the sake of the women and children and we journeyed not upon the Shabbath day nor upon any of the qodesh days, for we thought it better to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim according to the pattern of the shamayim than to proceed rapidly upon our way, and we did know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 prospered us in our journey and protected us from the power of all our enemies because we did faithfully serve Him and worship before His throne according to the divine pattern.
29.2: But at length we did arrive in the land of Shin’ar at the city of Ur.
29.3: Now the size of this city was immense.
29.4: Its buildings were grand and beautiful with gardens upon the rooftops and rivers of water running down from level to level.
29.5: The streets were wide and smooth and the inhabitants wealthy, dwelling in luxury.
29.6: Merchant caravans continually entered and left her gates and the great of all nations came here to pay homage to the mighty Meleḵ Nimroḏ.
29.7: Nevertheless, the wealth of this great city was built upon sin for the people served many mighty ones and offered upon their altars men, women, and children after the same manner as the Mitsrites.
29.8: And they had numerous slaves who were kept down in bondage and poverty and were driven like dumb beasts to provide the luxury in which their masters dwelt.
29.9: Behold, the inhabitants of the city did delight in whoredom and adultery and murder and all manner of evil, whereby they might get gain.
29.10: And the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was kindled against them.
29.11: Nevertheless, He did let them go on that they might be fully ripened in iniquity before the fullness of his wrath should fall upon them.
29.12: All of these things did 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim show unto me in a dream on the night before we entered into the city of Ur; and He said unto me, Aḇram, this city is vile and corrupt, but in it are some few beings who have not bowed the knee to their mighty ones and it is because of their prayers that I have brought you here, that they might be taught to worship the true Elohim after the order of the shamayim and be led out from wickedness and bondage.
29.13: Wherefore, go unto yours father’s house, for your mother has sorrowed for these many years, and I have softened the heart of your father toward these that he shall make you welcome and will protect these against the anger of the meleḵ such that you shall be able to accomplish your mission.
29.14: Behold, Aḇram, I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers Shĕm and Noaḥ, and of all the righteous fathers back to Aḏam.
29.15: Wherefore, I will remain with you and confirm upon you all the bireḵoth of the Fathers and you shall stand at the head of a multitude. Amĕn.

3.1: My father Teraḥ was the son of Naḥor and Naḥor was the son of Seruḡ and Seruḡ was the son of Re’u and Re’u was the son of Peleḡ in those days the earth was divided.
3.2: Peleḡ was the son of Ĕḇer who was the son of Shelaḥ who was the son of Arpaḵshaḏ the son of Shĕm, who was Malkitseḏeq, which by interpretation is meleḵ kohĕn, for he was a meleḵ and a kohĕn of the Most High Elohim.

30.1: In the morning before entering the city, I gathered my family together consisting of my seven wives, my fifty daughters, my twelve adopted sons, and three hundred and fifty menservants whom Shĕm had sent with their families, being in all six thousand three hundred and seventy beings.
30.2: And I said unto them, Behold, this great city is filled with wickedness and sin for the secret combinations that existed from the beginning still control it.
30.3: Wherefore, you shall remain here under the direction of Eli’ezer while I go alone into the city to my father’s house, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Shĕm and of Noaḥ has promised me that He will protect me against the anger of the meleḵ such that I shall be able to accomplish my mission.
30.4: I led my family in prayer before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, kissed them all and departing from them, entered into the city.

31.1: Being led by the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I found my father’s house, and entering the gate, addressed the guard who was standing there, saying, Behold, I am Aḇram, son of Teraḥ, who has spent these forty years in the house of Shĕm.
31.2: Take me now to my father.
31.3: The guard stood as one dumbfounded, knowing not what to make of such a greeting, but at length called a boy whom he dispatched to locate my father.
31.4: At length the lad returned, followed closely by my father who was greatly surprised to see me, but who recognized me as his son by the inspiration of the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.5: By this time my arrival had caused great excitement throughout my father’s household, which was very large, and my mother, having heard of my coming, hastened to the place where we were, weeping and rejoicing for she had thought that I had wandered from the cave and been slain by wild beasts in the wilderness.
31.6: At length she led me away to her chamber to talk with me and I told her of all that had transpired with me since my leaving the cave of my being led by the messenger to the city of Shalom, of being instructed under the direction of Shĕm, of the increase of my family and of the mercies of the true Elohim of the shamayim exercised in my behalf.
31.7: I talked to her of the futility of worshipping mighty ones of wood and stone made by men’s hands which have no power in them and of the Order of the Ancients which was preserved in the city of Shalom under Noaḥ and Shĕm which I had been sent to proclaim in the great city of Ur.

32.1: My mother heard all my words and rejoiced in them for she was one whose heart had been turned from the worship of dumb mighty ones to the worship of the unknown Elohim.
32.2: Moreover, a small body of like believers numbering about one hundred beings met secretly in my father’s house to worship the unseen Elohim and pray for further light concerning His Ways, among whom were my brother Haran, with his son Lot and his daughters Milkah and Sarai, and my brother Naḥor.
32.3: Now, when my mother had heard my words, she bade me remain with her until evening when the believers were to meet in her rooms.
32.4: Wherefore, that night I met with those who had rejected the idolatry of their fathers and they were all of the seed of those who had come out from the city of Peleḡ.
32.5: Wherefore, I rehearsed to them all the things I had told to my mother and they likewise rejoiced therein.
32.6: But unto my father I spake not of these things at this time for he was yet privy to Nimroḏ and was steeped in his evil ways.

33.1: When I had dwelt in my father’s house for seven days teaching the word of ḥai to the believers, I went to my father as he sat in his outer court with his servants attending to affairs of state.
33.2: And when he would hear me, I said unto him, father, where is the Elohim who created the shamayim and earth and all the hosts of them?
33.3: My father Teraḥ answered me and said, Behold, my son, those mighty ones who created all things are here with us in the house.
33.4: My father, show them to me I pray you; I exclaimed.
33.5: Whereupon my father Teraḥ led me unto a chamber in the center of his house wherein were twelve great mighty ones and numerous smaller ones.
33.6: And my father said to me, Behold, my son, these twelve great ones are rulers among the mighty ones and this largest one is ruler above all and these others were their assistants in creating all things.
33.7: And my father Teraḥ bowed down and worshipped before his mighty ones and we departed from them.

34.1: When I departed from the presence of my father, I went to my mother and said to her, My mother, there is a great evil in this place for my father kept a room full of mighty ones in the center of his house which thing is contrary to the Commandments of Elohim, wherefore the wrath of Elohim shall not depart from this house until they are destroyed.
34.2: Let one of the young men be sent, therefore, to fetch a kid of the goats and make thereof savory meat for therewith shall I destroy these mighty ones in which is neither life nor power.
34.3: My mother, therefore, summoned one of the young men who was with her in the house and sent him to fetch a kid of the goats whereof she made savory meat.
34.4: When it was prepared, I took the savory meat from her and went to the room where my father kept his mighty ones and I prayed there to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim saying, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Shĕm and of Noaḥ, look upon me here in my weakness and strengthen mine arm that I may destroy these false mighty ones and give me the wisdom and strength to go through all that follows and endure to the end in service to my Elohim.
34.5: When I had said these words, the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon me, even the Ruaḥ of Neḇuah, and I was led to exclaim, Woe to my father and this wicked and corrupt people among whom he dwells, whose hearts are all inclined to vanity, for they serve mighty ones of wood and stone, the workmanship of their own hands, which neither eat nor smell nor hear nor speak, for there is no power in them and those who serve them shall likewise be powerless to escape when the wrath of Elohim shall overtake them in a day they think not.

35.1: At this time the Ruaḥ of Elohim fell upon me in mighty power to strengthen mine arm, and picking up a hatchet which I had brought with me for that purpose, I destroyed all my father’s mighty ones, both wood and stone, by the power of Elohim which was in me, except for the largest in whose hand I placed the hatchet.
35.2: Then going to my father I said to him, My father, I have seen a wondrous thing for my mother did make me savory meat this day to offer before the mighty ones who created all things.
35.3: And when I took the meat into them, they all reached forth their hands to partake thereof.
35.4: When the one who is ruler above all saw their words, he being angered left the room and returned with a hatchet wherewith he destroyed the other mighty ones, both wood and stone; and behold, he stands there even now with the hatchet in his hand and the savory meat before him.

36.1: Hearing these words, my father hastened into the room of his mighty ones and found it even as I had said, and his anger was kindled against me and he said, This is an idle tale you have told me and false.
36.2: Why have you done this thing and lied to me?
36.3: These mighty ones have no life in them to do these things for they are wood and stone, and behold, I myself have had them made by the craftsmen.
36.4: Why have you then come into my house to destroy my mighty ones?

37.1: The Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon me at this time that I should answer my father and I said to him, How is it that you serve these mighty ones of wood and stone, the handiwork of the craftsmen in which is neither life nor power to act?
37.2: Can these which cannot deliver themselves from the hatchet deliver you from the power of the enemy?
37.3: Can they hear your prayers when you call upon them from out of the midst of your afflictions?
37.4: Surely it is an evil thing that you and your people should serve these false mighty ones, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, He is the Elohim who created the shamayim and earth and all that in them is, and He has commanded all men to worship Him only and to serve Him all their days.
37.5: Behold, your fathers in the days before the great flood worshipped false mighty ones after the same evil combination into which you have entered, and because of their perversions, they were destroyed.
37.6: Will you also go on in their wickedness to bring down the wrath of the Most High Elohim upon you that ye, too, should be destroyed from under the shamayim?
37.7: No, my father, but repent of this evil and turn unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and live.
37.8: So saying, I took the hatchet from the hands of the remaining mighty ones and smote him with it until he was destroyed.

38.1: My father, hearing my words and seeing what I had done, increased in anger against me and hastened from his house to the meleḵ, for he had access to Meleḵ Nimroḏ both day and night.
38.2: When he had entered the melaḵim’s presence, he bowed down before him and he said to him, My meleḵ, fifty years ago a man-child was born to my wife Amthelo, and when he was ten years old, we went on the new Moon to worship our ancestral mighty one when my son wandered off into the desert and was lost.
38.3: But he was found by the people of the desert and raised by them and he has recently found his way back into my house and I have received him with honor as my son.
38.4: Notwithstanding this, he did this day enter into the room of my mighty ones and destroy them and has spoken against our mighty ones and against that ancient order which has been handed down from our first father whereunto we are called.
38.5: Now, therefore, my meleḵ, send for him that he may be judged according to our law that this evil may be put away from among us.
38.6: The meleḵ thereupon sent three of his mighty men who fetched me from my father’s house and brought me before the meleḵ.

39.1: When I appeared before Meleḵ Nimroḏ, he was seated upon his throne in all his splendor, but it was as darkness to me.
39.2: At his right hand sat my father Teraḥ and around them sat the princes and noble ones of his realm.
39.3: And the meleḵ said to me, What is this thing that your father said to me, that you did this day enter into the room of his mighty ones and destroy them and that you have spoken against our mighty ones and against that ancient order which has been handed down from our first father whereunto we are called?

4.1: Noaḥ was the son of Lemeḵ, the son of Methushelaḥ, the son of Ḥanoḵ, who was taken up with his city that they might minister unto those in the flesh who sought a higher law than was available to them on the earth.
4.2: Now the birth of Noaḥ was after this manner: While his father Lemeḵ was journeying toward his home from preaching the Besorah among the sons of men, most of whom had rejected his testimony, a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared unto him and saluted him, saying, Hail Lemeḵ, you favored one of Elohim, for according to the promise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim to your father Ḥanoḵ, you have been chosen to be father to him through whom the seed of man will be preserved through the great flood which Elohim will send upon the earth in judgment, for all the sons of men have gone astray through the corruptions of those messengers who fell from among the shamayim and mingled their seed with the daughters of men and begat sons of great strength and mighty wickedness.
4.3: Yea, these have caused all flesh to corrupt their way before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; wherefore they shall be destroyed, save your son who shall be the seed of the future generations.

40.1: I answered the meleḵ saying, Why do you go on in wickedness to worship these dumb mighty ones in which there is no power even to save themselves?
40.2: Not only this, but you have led others to worship them and to enter into that order which is most abominable in the eyes of the Most High Elohim, for your father from where it comes from is the devil and it is full of lies and blasphemies and all manner of evil that men should lie and murder to get gain.
40.3: Why will you not serve the Most High Elohim who created all things in the shamayim and on earth, who has created these and holds the power to sustain your life or to destroy you?
40.4: O foolish, ignorant, wicked meleḵ, woe shall be unto you forever and ever for you are the son of Perdition for it is he who is your father.
40.5: You have corrupted the earth with your sins and with the sins of your people who follow you.
40.6: It was for entering into this wicked combination to get gain that your ancestors were destroyed in the flood when only eight beings were saved.
40.7: Will you and your people follow in their paths?
40.8: Then the wrath of the Most High Elohim will descend upon you to smite you from before His face.
40.9: Now put away these evil ways and turn to the Most High Elohim and serve Him that there may be hope for you.
40.10: But behold, I see that your heart is hardened in iniquity that there is no repentance for you, for the evil one has sealed those who are his; wherefore all your ways shall come to naught and you and your people shall be destroyed from off the face of the earth.

41.1: Then I lifted up my hands to the shamayim and prayed saying, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, You who sees all the ways of the wicked and will bring every evil deed into judgment, look upon these evil ones and destroy them that the whole earth be not corrupted by them and brought to destruction.

42.1: When the meleḵ heard my words and the prayer which I uttered, he ordered me to be cast into the prison house until he had determined what to do with me.
42.2: And after ten days, the meleḵ gathered together all his counselors and rehearsed to them all things concerning me.
42.3: And when he had rehearsed all things to them, he asked them, saying, What judgment shall such one receive who has reviled the meleḵ and our mighty ones and our qodesh order?
42.4: And they returned judgment to him saying, The man who reviled the meleḵ should be hanged from a tree until he is dead and the tree then shall be cut to the ground while all the people shall shout, Thus shall it befall him who reviled the meleḵ.
42.5: But this man has not only reviled the meleḵ but also our mighty ones and our qodesh order, and according to our law, such one shall be cast into a furnace of fire until he be consumed that nothing remains of him in the earth.
42.6: Let therefore the fire be increased in the meleḵ’s furnace which is in Kasdim where the meleḵ’s bricks are made and let this blasphemer be cast into the fire that he be consumed.

43.1: The meleḵ so commanded and for three days and three nights was the fire preparing in Kasdim and at the end of that time I was brought forth from the prison to be cast therein.
43.2: Nevertheless, while I was in the prison 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent His messengers to minister to me and to comfort me and they said to me, Fear not, Aḇram, for your work is not yet finished for you shall yet become the father of many nations and you shall preach the Besorah in far places, even in the land of Mitsrayim shall you declare the mysteries of your Elohim.
43.3: And though they cast you into the furnace, is not 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 able to deliver you therefrom?
43.4: For through your deliverance shall many be brought to bow down and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and forsake the evils of Nimroḏ.

44.1: Therefore, I came forth from the prison confident in the power of my Elohim and in His promise that I should be delivered from the fire.
44.2: But as I came forth, the astrologers of the meleḵ looked upon me and by the power of ha’Satan they recognized me, for they saw me clothed in light.
44.3: And they cried out unto the meleḵ saying, O meleḵ of all the earth, surely this is the man of whom we spake to you fifty years ago that he should rise up to overthrow your reign.

45.1: Hearing these words, the meleḵ was greatly troubled, and calling my father Teraḥ before him, he exclaimed, is this then your son who was to have been slain?
45.2: And what child then did I slay at his birth?
45.3: Speak now the truth and you shall go free; but if you speak not the truth, you shall die with your son.
45.4: And Nimroḏ caused my father to swear concerning the matter.

46.1: And my father answered the meleḵ saying, My meleḵ, I am guilty.
46.2: For because of my tender feelings toward my son, I did substitute for him the son of my concubine who was born on the same night.
46.3: The meleḵ’s wrath mounted and in his anger he cried, Who advised you to do this thing?
46.5: My father, being terrified at the melaḵim’s anger said, It was my son Haran who so advised me.
46.6: Now Haran had not advised my father of anything, but the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had wrought upon my father that he was loathe to give me up to the meleḵ.
46.7: Nevertheless, Haran was privy to what my father had done and Haran was one of the believers in the true Elohim of the shamayim, but his heart was not firm nor his faith sure.
46.8: Wherefore, Haran said in his heart, If Aḇram be delivered from the furnace, then shall I know that the Elohim of Aḇram is indeed the true Elohim.
46.9: Wherefore, Haran wavered in his faith and his confidence waxed not great in the Most High Elohim, but my confidence was secure, for I knew that it rested upon the Rock of my deliverance and that the Word of Elohim failed not.

47.1: Now when the meleḵ heard the words of my father, he caused that Haran should also be taken with me, and leading us to the valley of Kasdim, they stripped us of all our clothing and bound us with cords and cast us into the fire.
47.2: Now Haran, because his faith was not perfect in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim, was consumed in the fire that no trace of his body remained, but my faith remained firm in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and He sent His messengers to sustain me and release me from my bonds and I was three days and three nights in the furnace with the messengers, conversing with them and being instructed by them.

48.1: After the third day, the meleḵ sent his servants to govern the fire that it might again be used for making brick.
48.2: But when they came up to the furnace, behold, I was sitting therein conversing with the messengers whom Elohim had sent.
48.3: Therefore, the servants of the meleḵ, being greatly astonished, went and told him of this matter, but he would not believe them.
48.4: However, when the men persisted in their tale and showed great consternation, Meleḵ Nimroḏ himself came unto the furnace, but the messengers had departed and I sat alone in the flames.
48.5: When he saw me therein unconsumed, the meleḵ cried out in alarm, O Aḇram, are you a sorcerer greater than ours that you should live in the flames unconsumed?
48.6: But I answered him, Not so, O meleḵ, but Elohim of the shamayim who is the true Elohim above all has sent His messengers to me and has preserved me from this fire.
48.7: Being much amazed the meleḵ exclaimed, Come forth then from the fire for I see that no power of mine can harm you.

49.1: Whereupon, I ascended from the furnace and stood before the meleḵ and his counselors who examined me closely, but behold, even my hair was not singed.
49.2: Wherefore, the meleḵ caused garments from his own wardrobe to be brought and I was clothed therein and he caused me to be seated upon a throne at his right hand where my father used to sit and he said to me, What of Haran your brother who was cast into the furnace with you?
49.3: Did the messengers carry him away to some far place that he might be saved?
49.4: But I replied unto him, No, but the faith of my brother was not perfect in the Most High Elohim; wherefore he was consumed in the flames.
49.5: Upon hearing this, the meleḵ marveled and permitted me to speak in his court concerning the Most High Elohim and the redemption which should be wrought in behalf of those who believed on His Name.
49.6: Nevertheless, the heart of the meleḵ was not changed, for he gloried in power and he thought to learn from my power by permitting me to speak.
49.7: But about three hundred men of those who sat in the meleḵ’s court were converted to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and followed no more after the evil order of Nimroḏ, wherefore, they were cast out of the meleḵ’s presence; but as for me, the meleḵ gave me many gifts and sent me away in peace and many were joined to the believers in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from that day.
49.8: For having heard of my deliverance from the fire, multitudes came to my father’s house to hear of Elohim who could do such mighty things and many were converted unto the truth.

5.1: The mother of Noaḥ was also the daughter of Methushelaḥ for Lemeḵ and his wife had the same father but different mothers.
5.2: And when Noaḥ was born, his body was full of light, which thing caused great consternation to his father and mother and his father’s wives and children and all his house.
5.3: Moreover, the child stood upon his feet when he had come forth from the womb and his tongue was loosed and he did sing praises unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saying, I will praise you, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for you are the source of all power, the wellspring from which it flows to the sons of Elohim, and you are also abounding in wisdom and great and mighty counsel unto your servants.
5.4: Nevertheless, though you are Elohim who is long-suffering in judgment, the sins of the children of men have come up before your face and your fury has waxed strong and will be visited with judgments upon the earth.
5.5: Your mercies, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are beyond number, but you are Elohim that visited wrongdoing upon the children of men who the fullness of their iniquity has come upon them.
5.6: Therefore shall the earth be destroyed according to the word of Elohim which cannot fail. For the waters of the flood shall come upon the earth and all things shall perish from before your face, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
5.7: Nevertheless, in You do we put our trust for in whatsoever You do, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, you have always done justly. Amĕn.

50.1: Now, among the believers were Lot, the son of Haran, and Haran’s daughters, Milkah and Sarai.
50.2: Milkah was fair, but Sarai was beautiful above all women.
50.3: Her face was as that of a messenger filled with light, her cheeks as two roses in full bloom, her hair as spun gold which men treasure above all, her eyes as pools of blue reflecting the praise of Elohim’s sky, her nose delicate and lovely, and her countenance truly was fair as the sun.
50.4: Her breasts like two mountains rising above the plain of Shin’ar were fair to behold, and her complexion truly like the clouds in purity.
50.5: Her arms were comely, her hands perfect and delightful to behold, always in the service of those in need and quick to hasten to the service of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 her Elohim.
50.6: Her palms were lovely, unmarred by her constant labor, her fingers long and slender.
50.7: Her feet were comely and always set in the path of truth.
50.8: Her thighs were well-rounded and soft, yet never failing to sustain her in her labor of love in behalf of the servants of Elohim.
50.9: Truly no maiden was fairer than Sarai, the daughter of Haran, for her beauty was greater than all other women and she excelled them all.
50.10: But with her beauty was great wisdom and perfect faith in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and constant service in behalf of the qodeshim, for her hands never cease to baraḵ the people of Elohim.
50.11: Wherefore, my brother Naḥor took Milkah, the daughter of Haran, to wife, but I Aḇram, took Sarai at the direction of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and I found great joy in her.

51.1: But, behold, ha’Satan was not content to have me continue to disrupt his reign in peace; therefore, he sent a dream unto meleḵ Nimroḏ in which the meleḵ did see that I should be the destruction of himself and of his reign.
51.2: Moreover, it was shown the meleḵ in his dream that three of his own household, even Zeptah, Lilith, and Nefritiri, daughters to Onitah, the son of Nimroḏ, who were virgins, had joined the believers of the Most High Elohim.
51.3: When the meleḵ awoke from his sleep, he was angry and he caused that I, with these three virgins, Zeptah, Lilith, and Nefritiri, should be seized and bound and carried to Photiphar’s hill at the head of the plain of Olishem to be sacrificed unto the mighty one of Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim.
51.4: And these three virgins did the priest of Pharaoh offer up upon the altar and they died singing praises to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and bearing witness to the truth, wherefore, they shall be beruḵoth forever for they have entered into the rest of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

52.1: And when these virgins were slain, the priests of Pharaoh took me also and laid me upon the altar to slay me. But I cried unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim for I knew that my mission was not yet ended.
52.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard my voice and sent His messenger to loose the cords wherewith I was bound.
52.3: And I saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 seated upon His throne and He said to me, Aḇram, Aḇram, behold, My Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and I have heard you and have come down to deliver you and to take you away from your father’s house and from all your kindred into a land which is unknown to you, a land which I have promised to Noaḥ should be an eternal inheritance unto the promised seed.
52.4: Behold, I will lead you by My hand and will put upon you My Name that you shall bear the kehunnah of the fathers and the power thereof.
52.5: As it was with Noaḥ, so shall it be with you that through your ministry and the ministry of your seed bearing this kehunnah, My Name shall be known in the earth forever, for I am your Elohim.
52.6: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 broke down the altar of the idol mighty ones by an earthquake and smote their priests that they were all destroyed.

53.1: But I hastened to my father’s house where all the believers were gathered, fasting and praying for me and I said to them, Up, for this day we shall depart from this city that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 may visit it in wrath and vengeance.
53.2: Wherefore, all the believers gathered together and followed me out of the city to my camp.
53.3: And we struck our tents and departed from the land of Shin’ar to go to the city of Shalom to confer with father Shĕm.
53.4: And my father also, seeing that the meleḵ’s face would be set against him, gathered together his goods and followed after me.
53.5: We journeyed slowly, for I had with me many beings, both women and children and women with child.

54.1: When at length we arrived at the city of Shalom, father Shĕm came forth to greet us, bearing bread and wine which he baraḵ and gave to us and he said to me, Baruḵ are you, Aḇram, for the Most High Elohim has multiplied you and behold, your seed shall be even as the sand upon the seashore without number.
54.2: Go now with this great multitude into the land of Kena’an for to you and your seed will I give this land for an everlasting inheritance, said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim Almighty. Amĕn.

55.1: Thus we departed from the presence of Shĕm and moved to the vicinity of Ludor which city we denominated Ḥaran.
55.2: And we dwelt in the suburbs of Ḥaran for three years for there was much pasture there and a space large enough for the multitude which accompanied me.
55.3: And I preached the Besorah in Ḥaran and many beings were added unto the faithful in that place.

56.1: And there was a famine in the land, but the land of Ḥaran was baruḵ for our sakes that the famine there was light.
56.2: But at the end of three years, the famine abated throughout the land; wherefore Lot, my brother’s son, and I went before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in prayer after the manner of the ancients, and in answer to our prayer 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared unto me and said, Arise, Aḇram, and take Lot with you and all who follow after you, for I have purposed to take you out of Ḥaran and to make of you a minister to bear My Name in a strange land which I will give to your seed after you for an everlasting possession when they hearken to my voice.
56.3: For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Your Elohim.
56.4: I dwell in the shamayim; the earth is My footstool for I shall surely walk upon it when I come to redeem My people from their sins.
56.5: My Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and I know the end from the beginning; therefore, My hand shall be over you and I will make of you a great nation and I will baraḵ you above measure and make your name great among all nations and you shall be a beraḵah unto your seed after you, that in their hands they shall bear this ministry and kehunnah, even the kehunnah of the fathers after the Qodesh Order of Elohim, unto all nations.
56.6: And I will baraḵ all them, even as many as shall receive this Besorah through your name, for they shall be called after your name, even the seed of Aḇram, as though they were the seed of your own flesh, and they shall rise up and baraḵ you as their father.
56.7: For I will baraḵ them who baraḵ you and curse them who curse you.
56.8: In you, through the kehunnah which you bare, and in your seed, through your kehunnah which they shall bear which comes down from the fathers, shall all the families of the earth be baruḵ with the bireḵoth of the Besorah which are the bireḵoth of deliverance, even of eternal ḥai.
56.9: For I give you this promise, that your seed shall sprinkle all nations that through them the right to this kehunnah may encompass all mankind, that all may be brought into the covenant through obedience to the Torah and ordinances of the Besorah.

57.1: Now when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had ceased speaking with me, I praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saying, Your servant has sought You earnestly; now have I found You.
57.2: You did send these messengers to deliver me from death many times; shall I not do all things which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim required of me?
57.3: Baruḵ are You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who bestows Your love without measure upon the righteous but hates all iniquity.
57.4: But I have kept Your statutes to walk therein and have received Your ordinances unto myself, wherein You have baraḵ me with the Ruaḥ of knowledge and truth.
57.5: For my part, I will love You freely with all my heart and being.
57.6: I will cleave to You qodesh Torah to not turn aside therefrom in all You have commanded.
57.7: I have learned through the gift of Your Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh that no man is able to choose his own way nor direct his own steps for all such will fall into the pit.
57.8: In Your hand is the shaping of each man’s being which You have foreordained to conform to the image of Your Bĕn.
57.9: Wherefore, I will embrace the Bĕn and call upon Elohim for mercy for evermore. Amĕn.

58.1: Therefore, I took Sarai and Lot and all my family and all Lot’s family and all the beings who had joined us in Ur and in Ḥaran who would come and we departed out of the land of Kena’an.
58.2: But my father had departed not from his idolatry; wherefore, he remained in the land of Ḥaran and Naḥor also remained with some others who departed not from the truth of the living Elohim.

59.1: When we had come into the land of Kena’an, I built an altar in the plains of Moreh and offered sacrifice unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
59.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared unto me and said, This is the land which I will give to you and to your seed after you forever.
59.3: I will make your seed like the stars of the shamayim and I will give to them for an inheritance all the land which belonged to the Kena’anites for surely I will destroy them from off the face for the land when their wickedness is full.
59.4: Wherefore, I praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for His mercy and we departed from that place and journeyed toward Bĕyth Ĕl.

6.1: These things were a source of amazement and concern unto Lemeḵ who thereupon went unto his father, Methushelaḥ, and finding him in the Hĕyḵal he said, My father, this day did my wife, your daughter, bear a man child.
6.2: And at his birth the room was full of light so that we could not look upon him and when we could look upon him, behold, the child’s hair was white and fire seemed to come from his eyes and then he stood upon his feet and sang a hymn of praise unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and lo, he seemed to have the tongue of a messenger.
6.3: Tell me now the meaning of these things and how can I raise such a son?

60.1: And when I reached Ḥeḇron, I tarried there for two years, but the famine again waxed great in the land.
60.2: Hearing that there was no famine in Mitsrayim, I determined to journey into that land, remembering the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to me in Ur that I should declare the mysteries of my Elohim in the land of Mitsrayim.
60.3: And, behold, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ us on our journey that it was made light unto us and we journeyed until we reached the Kirmyon, one of the branches of the river of Mitsrayim, where we rested from our journey for a season, for here the famine was not so severe.
60.4: But remembering the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim to me, when we were recovered from our journey, I determined to move forward across the seven branches of the river of Mitsrayim into the heart of the country of the Mitsrites.

61.1: But on the night before I entered into Mitsrayim, I dreamed a dream.
61.2: And behold, in my dream I saw a cedar and a palm tree and the branches of the palm tree were wrapped around the cedar.
61.3: Suddenly, a group of men approached, seeking to cut down the cedar and leave the palm tree to stand alone.
61.4: But the palm tree cried out saying, Cut not down the cedar for whosoever seeks to cut it down shall find the curse of Elohim resting upon him.
61.5: So the men desisted and the cedar was spared by the act of the palm tree.

62.1: When the dream was ended, I awoke from my sleep and wondered at it.
62.2: Wherefore, I went before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in prayer and besought Him saying, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, show me the interpretation of this dream which I have had this night.
62.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, Behold, Sarai your wife is a beautiful woman to look upon above all the women of the earth.
62.4: Therefore, it shall come to pass that when the Mitsrites shall see her, they will say, She is his wife, and they will seek to slay you for the sake of obtaining your wife.
62.5: Let Sarai your wife, therefore, say to them, He is my kinsman, and your being shall live.
62.6: For you are the cedar, O Aḇram, and Sarai is the palm tree and this is the interpretation of the dream; for through the act of your wife, you shall be saved and the way will be opened for you to preach the mysteries of reverence in the court of Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim, for these Mitsrites are your kindred of the seed of Ĕḇer, and it is My Will that the truths of the everlasting Besorah should be brought to them.

63.1: Now I had heard while I dwelt in Ḥaran that some of seed of Ĕḇer had entered into Mitsrayim and driven the seed of Ḥam to the south and taken possession of the land.
63.2: But these followed not after the Elohim of their father Ĕḇer, but worshipped mighty ones, even as did my father Teraḥ, but they followed not after the abominations of Nimroḏ.
63.3: Now these Iḇri were of the seed of Haḏoram, the son of Yoqtan, the son of Ĕḇer.
63.4: And Yoqtan was the brother of Peleḡ.
63.5: And Ĕḇer was the son of Shelaḥ, the son of Arpaḵshaḏ, the son of Shĕm.
63.6: Wherefore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had sent me to preach the Besorah to these who had departed from the Elohim of their fathers.

64.1: Wherefore, I awakened my wife Sarai and I said to her, I have had a dream of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
64.2: Tell it to me, she said, that I may know what it is.
64.3: Therefore, I related to her the dream and all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said to me concerning it and I added, When the men of the land shall inquire of you saying, Who is this who accompanies you, say unto them simply, He is my kinsman.
64.4: Thus shall my being live and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will use their love for you as a means whereby the Besorah shall be preached among them.
64.5: Fear not to do this thing for they will neither defile you, contrary to your covenants, nor slay me, but all shall come to pass to the praise of our Elohim.

65.1: Sarai, my wife, was fearful when she heard of the danger through which we must pass and wept that night before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but she placed her trust in Him and was comforted by His Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.
65.2: The next day we moved on across the seven branches of the river and proceeded toward Foan where Pharaoh dwelt.
65.3: But I kept Sarai hidden until we reached Foan, for it was in the home of Pharaoh that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 purposed to use her great beauty to open the heart of Pharaoh unto the work of Elohim.
65.4: When we reached the city of Foan, three of Pharaoh’s officers met us and I brought Sarai forth to sit at my right hand while I gave them audience.
65.5: And according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, while I attempted to explain unto them our having come there because of the famine in the land of Kena’an and that we sojourned among them, they kept bestowing compliments upon Sarai for her great beauty and wisdom and the luster of her countenance.

66.1: When the men departed from me, they went directly into the presence of Pharaoh and when they had eaten with him, he had good wine brought forth.
66.2: While they drank together, they began to speak to him of what had transpired, but all they could speak of were the beauties of Sarai.
66.3: How beautiful is the woman Sarai, they said, who sits at Aḇram’s right hand.
66.4: How comely is the shape of her face; how delicate and finespun are her tresses.
66.5: How beautiful her eyes. How delicate is her nose and the whole luster of her countenance.
66.6: How fair are her breasts and how comely with all is her complexion.
66.7: How comely, too, are her arms and how perfect her hands.
66.8: How pleasing are her hands to behold; how lovely her palms, how long and slender her fingers.
66.9: How comely are her feet. How well rounded her thighs.
66.10: None of the maidens and none of the brides that enter the bridechamber are fairer than she.
66.11: Her beauty is greater than all other women and she excels them all.
66.12: Moreover, along with all this beauty, she has great wisdom and the workmanship of her hands is fair indeed.

67.1: When he heard these words, Pharaoh lusted after Sarai and he sent his servants to fetch her to him.
67.2: Knowing it to be the Will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I let her go although my heart was grieved within me.
67.3: When Pharaoh saw her, his lust grew within him, for he was overcome by her beauty and he took her into his household as his wife and sent men to slay me that I might not rise up to claim her.
67.4: But Sarai, seeing these things said unto Pharaoh, He is but my kinsman; wherefore, Pharaoh called back his men and my life was spared.

68.1: But Lot and I and all our household spent that night in prayer before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for Sarai that she might accomplish her mission and that she might not be defiled contrary to her covenants.
68.2: And I stood with my arms stretched out toward the shamayim after the Qodesh Order of Elohim and I said, Baruḵ are You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Most High Elohim, Aḏonai of all worlds and Aḏonai and Ruler over all things.
68.3: I know that You do rule over all the melaḵim of the earth, executing judgment upon them in righteousness even as You did save me from the evil designs of the mighty meleḵ Nimroḏ.
68.4: Now do I complain before You concerning Pharaoh of Foan, meleḵ of Mitsrayim, who has violently abducted my wife Sarai from me.
68.5: Wreak justice upon him in my behalf and let me behold Thine hand wax mighty against him and against all his household and let him not be able this night to defile my wife contrary to her covenants.
68.6: Let them come to know, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of all the melaḵim of the earth and the Ruler of all men, for this cause did I suffer Sarai to go among them according to Your counsel.

69.1: And Elohim hearkened unto my prayer and withheld His Ruaḥ from the Mitsrites that none of them were able to come at their wives that night.
69.2: In the morning, consternation reigned throughout the land of Mitsrayim, for no man had been able to lie with his wife all that night.
69.3: Pharaoh also was greatly perplexed, for although his lust toward Sarai had grown throughout the night, he had been unable to satisfy that lust because of the curse of Elohim which rested upon him.
69.4: Therefore, he summoned all of his wise men and the physicians of his household, but none could heal him and all had suffered the same affliction.

7.1: Hearing these words, Methushelaḥ, too, was troubled and said, Fear not, my son, for although I know not the meaning of these things, I will go unto my father, Ḥanoḵ, for he is privy to the messengers and he will be able to explain all things to us.
7.2: Whereupon, Methushelaḥ traveled to the top of the highest mountain where he could speak unto his father, Ḥanoḵ, and he said unto him, My father, my daughter, who is the wife of my son Lemeḵ, has this day brought forth a man-child.
7.3: And at his birth the room was full of light so that they could not look upon him and when they could look upon him, behold the child’s hair was white and fire seemed to come from his eyes and then he stood upon his feet and sang a hymn of praise unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and lo, he seemed to have the tongue of a messenger.
7.4: Thus said my son Lemeḵ, who is greatly perplexed as to the meaning of these things and how he can raise such a son.

70.1: Then the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon Sarai and she said, My master, it is indeed a sad matter that this affliction should be upon you.
70.2: My kinsman Aḇram is a man full of wisdom and of the Ruaḥ of our Elohim.
70.3: Send for him, therefore, and he shall tell you how to be delivered from these bonds that you may freely take me to yourself.
70.4: Now this she said at the direction of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 softened Pharaoh’s heart that he hearkened unto her words and he sent Shulem, one of his chief ministers, into my camp.

71.1: When Shulem arrived in camp, he was, according to my directions, went to the tent of Lot, and when he had entered the tent, he bowed before Lot and said, My master Pharaoh and all the males of the land of Mitsrayim have been cursed that they are unable to come at their wives.
71.2: But it has been told Pharaoh by his handmaiden Sarai that her kinsman Aḇram is a man full of wisdom and of the Ruaḥ of your Elohim.
71.3: Let him, therefore, come and lay his hands upon my master Pharaoh and pray for him that he may be healed and live.
71.4: But Lot said to him, As long as his wife Sarai remains with the meleḵ, my uncle Aḇram will not be able to pray for him.
71.5: Be off you and tell the meleḵ to release the woman to her husband.
71.6: Then he will pray for him and he will be healed.

72.1: When Shulem heard these words, he was amazed and he went straightway to the meleḵ.
72.2: My meleḵ, said he, This curse has come on account of Sarai the wife of Aḇram.
72.3: Let Sarai be but restored to her husband Aḇram and this curse will be lifted from off all the males of Mitsrayim.
72.4: Upon hearing these words, the meleḵ asked Sarai saying, Is this thing so?
72.5: Yea, my master, she replied, and it is done that you might behold the power of Elohim.
72.6: For when your heart lusted after me, you should have asked and not taken me by force.
72.7: But this is done that the praise of Elohim might be revealed that you should turn from the worship of dumb mighty ones to the worship of the true and living Elohim.

73.1: Hearing these words, Pharaoh summoned me to him and when I entered his presence he asked, What is this that has been done?
73.2: For I have taken Sarai to wife while she was yet your wife and for this thing a curse has fallen upon me and all males in the land of Mitsrayim.
73.3: Therefore, pray for me that this curse may be removed from us.
73.4: According to Pharaoh’s request, I laid my hands upon him and prayed over him and he and all the males of Mitsrayim were healed.

74.1: When the meleḵ had been baruḵ, he was recovered and he praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for his recovery.
74.2: Wherefore, I took him into his garden and immersed him in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and all his household with him.
74.3: And when I had baraḵ him again, Sarai came before him and he knew that he had been healed for the Ruaḥ of Elohim fell upon him with this testimony and the witness thereof was sure.

75.1: Then Pharaoh arose and praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and proclaimed to all his people that they should worship the Most High Elohim who had healed them.
75.2: And he desired to enter into a covenant of eternal brotherhood with me that I should be his father and he should be my son.
75.3: Wherefore, I said unto Pharaoh, Put forth your hand upon my thigh and I will make you swear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of the shamayim and earth, that you shall be true to me and your heirs to my heirs forever, and I shall receive you to myself to be my son and brother to inherit all the bireḵoth of my house and to bear my kehunnah forever.
75.4: Wherefore, Pharaoh put his hand upon my thigh and swore to me according to this oath.
75.5: And when he had sworn, Lot sealed him to me that he should be my son in time and eternity and Pharaoh rejoiced therein.

76.1: And the meleḵ clothed me in his own robes and seated me upon his throne, placing his own crown upon my head and his sceptre in my hand.
76.2: And I did teach him and his people in all the mysteries of reverence from first to last.
76.3: For Pharaoh did introduce me into the Hĕyḵal which had been built by the fathers, commenced by father Shĕth and completed by father Shĕm after the great flood and therein I did officiate in the rites and ordinances of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
76.4: And Pharaoh made all matters right with Sarai, and he baraḵ her with the outpouring of his spirit and she was beruḵah in his presence.
76.5: And he gave to her Haḡar, his own daughter, also, to be her companion and to Haḡar he gave many gifts.
76.6: And I was seven years in the land of Mitsrayim teaching the Besorah and administering to Pharaoh and his household and all the Mitsrites the bireḵoth, rites, and ordinances of the Besorah with the power thereof.
76.7: And I established among them the order of the fathers and the kehunnah thereof until the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was esteemed throughout the land of Mitsrayim.
76.8: And I taught the people the nature of the shamayim and of the earth and the plan of deliverance and the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 unto those who serve Him in purity of heart and to believe on the Bĕn of Elohim who should come to make an atonement for their sins.
76.9: And so great was the power of Elohim among us that in time all of the Mitsrites had turned from their idolatry to the worship of the true Elohim and I and my people had cause to rejoice in the fruits of labors.

77.1: At the end of seven years, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 visited me and he said to me, Baruḵ are you, Aḇram, servant of the Most High, for your joy shall be great in my mansion with this multitude which you have brought to me; wherefore, your name shall no more be called Aḇram but Aḇraham shall you be called, which is by interpretation, Father of a Multitude.
77.2: Moreover, your wife Sarai shall no longer be called by that name, but Sarah shall she be called, which signifies a Queen.
77.3: For Sarah have I chosen and appointed to be your queen of queens for from her shall issue the promised seed, even him who shall be your heir.
77.4: Behold, the day comes when the seed of Ḥam shall again rule in this land and at that day your seed shall be in bondage to them, but I will raise up a prince from among the Mitsrites who shall lead them out of bondage and they shall inherit the land of Kena’an, even that land which I have promised to you and to your seed after you for an everlasting inheritance.
77.5: Moreover, from the loins of you heir shall proceed ha’Mashiaḥ, even the Bĕn of Elohim, who shall walk upon the earth ministering to the poor and lowly, who shall be lifted up that the price might be paid for the original sin of Aḏam and for the sins of all mankind, that all who will believe on His Name and receive His ordinances and keep His Commandments should not perish but inherit everlasting life.
77.6: Moreover, in the last days I will raise up out of the loins of your heir a choice seer through whom the fullness of My Besorah shall be restored to the earth and all things shall be restored as in the beginning.
77.7: For upon Him shall rest the kehunnah of His fathers and He shall commence the organization of that qodesh order which was in the beginning of the world which shall be consummated before the Bĕn of Elohim shall walk again upon the earth.
77.8: These promises are yours, my son, and I say unto you, you shall be exalted and dwell with Me in the mansion of My Father.
77.9: Now take your people and return into the land of Kena’an, for there have I a mission for you and there shall the promises come to pass in your behalf.

78.1: When I had received this Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and He had departed from me, I went to Pharaoh and told him that I must depart from his realm as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had a work for me to do in the land of Kena’an.
78.2: Though he was loathe to see me go, Pharaoh bowed to the Will of Elohim and appointed men from his own bodyguard to escort me to the borders of Mitsrayim and he gave me gifts of cattle and silver and gold and fine cloth and precious jewels of every kind.

79.1: So I went up out of Mitsrayim and Lot accompanied me who had taken three wives while in Mitsrayim, namely, Yennifer, daughter of Eli’ezer of Dammeseq, Deḇorah, daughter of Kumen who had come out of the city of Ur, and Asterah, daughter of Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim.

8.1: Hearing this report, Ḥanoḵ comforted his son Methushelaḥ, saying, Fear not, my son, nor fret yourself about this matter for did not a qodesh messenger visit your son Lemeḵ and tell him that this should be the seed of the future generations? And was it not so?
8.2: For this cause have these things happened; but on the eighth day when the child is circumcised, he shall be covered and shall appear as other men except that his hair shall remain white as a token that through him 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will do a mighty work.
8.3: This word did Methushelaḥ return to his son Lemeḵ and he was comforted.

80.1: Traveling slowly and stopping often to camp upon our way, we eventually reached Bĕyth Ĕl, where yet stood an altar that I had built there at the first.
80.2: I restored it to its perfect form and offered sacrifices thereon to the Most High Elohim.
80.3: And I called there upon the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of all worlds and offered praise to the Name of Elohim and baraḵ Elohim and gave thanks before Him for all the possessions bestowed upon us and for the many beings we had won in Mitsrayim and for having brought us back safely from that land.

81.1: Now after our departure from Mitsrayim, a faction arose among our people upon seeing the great wealth which Pharaoh had entrusted to us, for they desired property which they could call their own.
81.2: Lot also was among them, which this thing grieved me greatly, but seeing they would not be reconciled, we gave to them a portion of the common property and they departed from us under Lot’s direction and settled in the Valley of the Yardĕn River.
81.3: There they went from place to place as their flocks needed pasture until they reached the city of Seḏom where they mingled with the inhabitants and became one with them.
81.4: Lot also built a house in Seḏom and settled there, but of all that company that went out from us, only Lot maintained his integrity and did not violate the covenants of his kehunnah nor bow to mighty ones.
81.5: Nevertheless, Lot did not walk perfectly in the Way of the Fathers for he dwelt not among the people of Elohim but built his own house and he coveted his own property that he should govern it rather than holding all things common with the qodeshim.
81.6: Nevertheless, Lot did continue to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loved him and his family and his property grew very large.
81.7: But I was grieved in my heart that Lot had parted from me for he had stood at my right hand and had been instructed in a better way.

82.1: Meanwhile, I with my people dwelt in Bĕyth Ĕl where we did worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim after the Order of the Ancients and did strive diligently to establish the Qodesh Order of Elohim among us in ever increasing perfection.
82.2: Wherefore, we did banish from among us all contention, all covetousness, all selfishness, and we were of one heart and of one mind and dedicated in all our service unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and held all things common, for no man called anything his own.

83.1: One-night Elohim appeared to me in a vision and said, Go up to the top of Ḥatsor and lift up your eyes and gaze eastward and westward and southward and northward and behold all this land for, behold, to you and to your seed after you shall I give it for an everlasting inheritance.
83.2: The next day I ascended Ḥatsor as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded me and I gazed upon all the land from the river of Mitsrayim unto Leḇanon and Senir, from the Great Sea unto Ḥawran, the whole area of Sĕ’ir as far as Qaḏĕsh, the whole of the great wilderness which lies east of the Ḥawran ran and the region of Senir as far as the Perath.
83.3: And as I beheld the land, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim spake in my heart, saying, Baruḵ Aḇraham, I have chosen you to stand at the head of a multitude.
83.4: Wherefore, to you and to your seed after you I will give this land, even all that your eyes behold, that you may possess it forever.
83.5: And I shall multiply you seed like the dust of the earth, for even as no man can count the dust of the earth, so shall your seed be without number.
83.6: Rise up, now, and compass this land.
83.7: Behold the length of it and the breadth of it, for I will give it to you and to your seed after you forever.

84.1: Even so, I, Aḇraham, descended from the high place and set out to behold all the land.
84.2: I commenced at the river of Mitsrayim and came to the shore of the lake beside which I traveled until I reached the mountain of the ox.
84.3: Then, I turned from the great lake which is by Seḏom and walked across the breadth of the land until I reached Perath.
84.4: Then, I journeyed even to the Sea of Reeds which I followed to its head.
84.5: Then, I went onward to the river of Mitsrayim again, having compassed the whole land according to the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
84.6: When I had completed my journey, I bowed down and praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and returned safely to my family where I found everyone well.

85.1: Not many days then, under the direction of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I departed from Bĕyth Ĕl and settled in the plains of Mamrĕ on the northeast of Ḥeḇron and there I built an altar and offered an offering to the Most High Elohim and dedicated that land unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
85.2: And I held a great feast to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the time of the Pesaḥ had come and together with all the men of my household, invited Mamrĕ, Aneram, and Eshkol, my friends who were wanderers in the land as we were and who had joined the believers in the Most High Elohim, into the Solemn Assembly.
85.3: And after this all my people ate and drank together with me before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

86.1: At this feast, the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon me and laying aside my garments, I danced before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and sang unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 a new song, saying, Baruḵ are You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who has given to man knowledge of Your Ways that he might understand Your truths and see Your abundant mercies.
86.2: Baruḵ are You, O Elohim, who are full of compassion and favor, for the greatness of Your power, the abundance of Your truth, the profusion of Your mercies over all Your works.
86.3: Rejoice the being of Your servant in Your truth and through Your righteousness make me clean before You.
86.4: Baruḵ are You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for You have placed in the mouth of Your servant the qodesh words of power that I might stand as Your minister continually that I may confer Your favor upon Your children and that I myself may return to Your presence.

87.1: Sarah also rose up, full of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, and danced and sang before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
87.2: And this is the song of Sarah: In You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, will my being be raised up for You have bestowed upon me Your favor whereby I am restored to Your presence for I have entered into Your Qodesh House and received the qodesh rites of Your presence.
87.3: Surely in my tent at night I will sing songs of joy to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as I am overshadowed by the kehunnah and lifted up in the foreshadowing of eternity.
87.4: Surely in receiving Your Ruaḥ through the overshadowing of the kehunnah, I have received deliverance.
87.5: Wherefore, in the midst of Your people, those who reverence Your Qodesh Name, I will praise You and esteem Your Name forever.

88.1: My wife Kadar also arose and proceeded to dance and sing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
88.2: And her song was: Baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O my being; exalt His Name among the people.
88.3: I will praise You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, upon my bed when the wellsprings of my joy are opened up.
88.4: I will praise You at all times and seasons.
88.5: When the sun rises upon the earth, I will praise Your Qodesh Name.
88.6: When in its ordered course, day reaches its turning point at the meridian, I shall not fail to praise You.
88.7: Again in the evening when the daylight departs, I will marvel at Your wonders and esteem Your Name.

89.1: Then rose up my wife Yahuḏith who danced and sang, saying, Praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who has shown me the wonders of His Ways.
89.2: For as I lay upon my bed enwrapped in the ecstasies of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, when the Ruaḥ rushed into me, I saw the vision of the Almighty and heard that which is unlawful to be spoken.
89.3: Yea, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You have visited me and I have heard Your wondrous secret and I know that it is true. Through Your Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, through the rites of Your qodesh kehunnah, through the radiant inner vision to which You did open my mind in the moment of passion, You have caused a spring of knowledge to well up within me, a fountain of strength and power, of loving kindness and splendor in my Elohim.
89.4: You have put an end to the darkness of the world in me and the splendor of Your praise has become in me an eternal light.
89.5: Wherefore, I will praise to Your Name forever and give myself unto You.

9.1: And on the eighth day when the child was circumcised, he was covered that he became as other men except that his hair remained white and they called his name Noaḥ, which by interpretation is comfort, because, Lemeḵ said, My heart is comforted to know that my seed shall be preserved through the great flood.

90.1: When Yahuḏith had finished her song, all the congregation, being filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, arose to their feet and began to dance and sing and praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and to neḇuah in His Name.
90.2: Some saw qodesh messengers in our midst and others saw the shamayim opened and beheld Elohim seated upon His throne and all were filled with His Ruaḥ and shouted praises to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in joyousness until dawn.
90.3: Then we all rose up before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and praised His Name for this great outpouring and worshipped Him all that day.
90.4: And we rejoiced in the favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.

91.1: Previous to this time, Amraphel, son of Nimroḏ, meleḵ of Shin’ar, Keḏorla’omer, meleḵ of Ĕylam, Aryoḵ, meleḵ of Ellasar, and Tiḏ’al, meleḵ of Goyim in Paddan Aram, had waged war against Bera, meleḵ of Seḏom, Birsha, meleḵ of Amorah, Shinaḇ, meleḵ of Aḏmah, Shem’ĕḇer, meleḵ of Tseḇoyim, and the meleḵ of Bela.
91.2: They assembled for combat in the valley of Siddim and the meleḵ of Shin’ar and his royal allies overcame the meleḵ of Seḏom and his confederates and imposed tribute upon them.
91.3: For twelve years they paid their tribute to the meleḵ of Shin’ar, but in the thirteenth year they revolted against him.
91.4: In the fourteenth year the meleḵ of Shin’ar led forth all his allies and they went up along the way of the wilderness, attacking and plundering all who were confederate with the meleḵ of Seḏom.
91.5: But the meleḵ of Seḏom, the meleḵ of Amorah, the meleḵ of Aḏmah, the meleḵ of Tseḇoyim, and the meleḵ of Bela came forth to battle and met Amraphel and his allies in the valley of Siddim.
91.6: However, Amraphel and his allies prevailed against them and Bera, meleḵ of Seḏom turned and fled and Birsha, meleḵ of Amorah fell into the slime pits which were in the valley of Siddim and perished there.
91.7: The remainder of the melaḵim fled unto the mountain which was called Hanabal and tarried there in great fear.

92.1: But one of Lot’s servants who dwelt in his house escaped and came to me in Ḥeḇron and told me that Lot, my brother’s son, had been taken with all his possessions, but that he yet lived.
92.2: He showed me, moreover, the route which the melaḵim had taken toward the land of Dammeseq.
92.3: When I heard this news, my heart melted within me for Lot who had stood at my right hand had been as a brother to me in the place of my brother Haran, who had been slain in the Land of Shin’ar.
92.4: O, that Lot had stayed among the body of qodeshim of the Most High Elohim, I thought, and not go off to possess his own property apart.
92.5: Then these circumstances would never have befallen him that he should be in the hands of Amraphel, son of Nimroḏ, meleḵ of Shin’ar and his host.
92.6: But as I mourned over Lot, the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came unto me, saying, Up, arouse you, O Aḇraham. Take three hundred and eighty of the young men of the strength of your house and also your friends Aneram, Eshkol, and Mamrĕ each with one hundred and five of the strength of his house and also Eli’ezer of Dammeseq who is with you in the tent and pursue after Amraphel, son of Nimroḏ, meleḵ of Shin’ar, for truly I shall deliver his hosts into your hands.

93.1: Wherefore, we did according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded me, having all seven hundred men and we pursued after them even unto the valley of Dan where we found them encamped.
93.2: And falling upon them by night from all four directions, we commenced the work of death and continued wreaking slaughter among them and discomforting them all that night.
93.3: And with the rising of the sun, they fled from before us until they reached Ḥoḇah which is situated to the left of Dammeseq where we did again overtake them and conquer them.
93.4: There we did strip them of all that they had taken as plunder and loot and likewise of all their won goods.
93.5: Lot also and his family we rescued from their hands and restoring to him all his possessions and all that they had taken from him as spoil, we restored him to his home in peace.

94.1: When the meleḵ of Seḏom heard that I had returned from the conquest of Amraphel, son of Nimroḏ, meleḵ of Shin’ar, he came forth to meet me at the valley of Shawĕh which is west of the city of Shalom where Noaḥ and Malkitseḏeq dwelt.
94.2: And Malkitseḏeq brought forth bread and wine from the city of Shalom unto the valley of Shawĕh where we were encamped.
94.3: And he being the kohĕn ha’gadol after the Order of the Most High Elohim, break the bread and baraḵ it and he baraḵ the wine also and he distributed them unto me and those who were with me, and we partook and were filled.
94.4: And Malkitseḏeq lifted up his hands to the shamayim and baraḵ me, and said, Baruḵ Aḇraham, you are a man of the Most High Elohim, possessor of the shamayim and of earth, wherefore, His Name and kehunnah shall not depart from you and your seed after you while the earth shall stand and even in eternity shall it remain with you.
94.5: And baruḵ is the Name of the Most High Elohim and almighty His power, which has delivered your enemies into your hand.
94.6: And I, Aḇraham, gave into the hand of Malkitseḏeq, tithes of all I had taken, for he was the presiding kohĕn ha’gadol after the Order of the Most High Elohim, the first of the fathers to me, and he reigned under his father Noaḥ.

95.1: And when the meleḵ of Seḏom had come to me, he said to me, Aḇraham, give me the persons who are not your but who are with you whom you have rescued from the hand of Amraphel, son of Nimroḏ, meleḵ of Shin’ar, but let all the property be left with you.
95.2: But I said to him, This day do I, Aḇraham, lift up my hand before the Most High Elohim, before His qodesh messengers and before these witnesses who are with us and declare that I will not take even so much as a thread or a shoe’s latchet which is not mine, lest you should say that all Aḇraham’s wealth cometh really from their possession.
95.3: Only that which the young men who are with me have eaten and that which Aneram, Eshkol, and Mamrĕ, these three stalwarts who went with me, have received as their share shall be excepted of all that I took from Amraphel, son of Nimroḏ, meleḵ of Shin’ar that was thine.
95.4: The rest I return freely to you.
95.5: Now go your way in peace.
95.6: Thereupon, I returned all the possessions and all the spoil and gave them to the meleḵ of Seḏom and I released all the captives and sent them away rejoicing.

96.1: And when I had done this, Malkitseḏeq again lifted up his voice and baraḵ me saying, Baruḵ are you, Aḇraham, for the Most High Elohim shall visit you and shall bestow upon you riches and honor and lands for an everlasting possession because you have been true and faithful to the covenants which you have entered before Him.
96.2: Wherefore, you shall continue to increase, worlds without end, and the splendor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall never depart from you. The bireḵoth of your Fathers shall rest upon you and you shall stand at the head and in you and in your seed after you, those who shall bear the kehunnah, shall all the nations of the earth be baruḵ.

97.1: Therewith, I departed from Malkitseḏeq, rejoicing in his beraḵah, for he was a man of faith who wrought righteousness and as child he feared Elohim and by his faith he stopped the mouths of lions and quenched the violence of fire when those of the evil combination sought to destroy him from off the face of the earth.
97.2: Therefore, having been approved of Elohim, he was ordained a kohĕn ha’gadol after the order of the Covenant which Elohim made with Ḥanoḵ which is after the order of the First-born, even our Father Aḏam.
97.3: For this qodesh order came not by man nor the will of man, neither by father nor mother, neither by beginning of days nor end of years, but of Elohim.
97.4: For it was established in the beginning of the earth by the Ancients of days, wherefore it is called the Order of the Ancients, and it was delivered unto men from the beginning by the calling of Elohim’s own voice according to His own will through the voice of His kehunnah, to as many as believed on His Name and were faithful until they had obtained.

98.1: Behold, these could transcend the veil, according to the Will of Elohim, and commune with the General Assembly and Ekklesia of the First-born in the shamayim and many were caught up to be with them.
98.2: For Elohim had sworn to Ḥanoḵ and to his seed with an oath by Himself that every one being ordained after this order and calling should have power by faith to break mountains, to divide the seas, to dry up waters, to turn them out of their course, to put at defiance the armies of nations, to divide the earth, to break every band, to stand in the presence of Elohim, to do all things according to His Will according to His Command, subdue principalities and powers, and this by the Will of the Bĕn of the Only Begotten of the Father which was from before the foundation of the world.
98.3: And men having this faith and coming up unto this order of Elohim could be translated and taken up into the shamayim.

99.1: Now Malkitseḏeq was a kohĕn after this order which is the Qodesh Order of Elohim; therefore he obtained peace in Shalom and was called the prince of peace.
99.2: And his people wrought righteousness and obtained the shamayim for they sought for the city of Ḥanoḵ which Elohim had before taken, separating it from the earth, having reserved it unto the latter days or the end of the world.
99.3: For Elohim has said and sworn with an oath that the shamayim and the earth should come together again and the sons of Elohim be tried even by fire.
99.4: And thus Malkitseḏeq, having established righteousness, was called the meleḵ of the shamayim by his people or, in other words, the meleḵ of peace.
99.5: And they communed with those in the city of Ḥanoḵ and in the city of Peleḡ and had access to them and were baruḵ all their days.
